【先週のSNSでのエネルギー 2026/09/26】

アジア太陽光・蓄電市場の急拡大と日本の位置づけ：周辺地域の投資動向が示す構造的格差

---

▍このトピックが注目された背景

先週（9月17日）、アジア太平洋地域の再生可能エネルギー関連ニュースが相次ぎました。
インドでAlpex Solarがウッタル・プラデーシュ州マトゥラーに2.2GWのTOPCon太陽電池製造施設を開所
し、
バングラデシュでは屋上太陽光発電をはじめとする再生可能エネルギープロジェクト向けに1億2,300万ドルの基金を設立
、さらに
豪州ビクトリア州では州営電力会社SECが400MW／1.86GWhのBaranduda蓄電プロジェクトへ最大4,300万豪ドルを出資する合意
が報じられました。こうした案件が同日に重なったことで、国内外の再エネ推進動向を対比する言説がSNS上で急速に広がりました。

---

▍言説の構造と広がり

今回SNSで拡散した言説の核心は、「周辺アジア諸国が大規模投資を矢継ぎ早に打ち出している一方、日本の国内言説は批判・懸念に傾きがちである」という対比構造にあります。この種の言説が拡散しやすい背景には複数の要因があります。

第一に、数値の具体性です。「2.2GW工場稼働」「1.23億ドル基金」「1.86GWh着工」という数字は視覚的インパクトが強く、共有・引用が容易です。第二に、感情的な落差の利用です。他国の前進と国内の停滞という二項対立の構図は、人々の焦燥感や危機感を刺激しやすく、拡散を促します。第三に、「自国批判」という文脈への共感です。再エネ推進派・懐疑派いずれの立場からも、各々の論拠として援用しやすい情報構造を持っています。

ただし、こうした比較言説はしばしば細部の文脈を省略します。「工場稼働」という表現が企業名・技術種別・商業生産開始時期の詳細を省略している点、「着工確定」という表現が投資最終決定と物理的着工の区別を曖昧にしている点は、SNS上の言説として注意を要します。

---

▍データ・事実による検証

（1）インド：2.2GW工場稼働

インドの太陽光メーカーAlpex Solarが、マトゥラーのコシ・コトワン工業地区において2.2GW規模のTOPCon G12R太陽電池製造施設を開所しました。同施設はウッタル・プラデーシュ州初の統合型TOPConギガスケール製造ラインとされています。
これは「稼働（コミッション）」に相当する事実と確認されます。
同工場は発表から15か月以内に完成したとAlpex社は述べています。
この工場稼働は、インドの製造基盤の急速な拡大という大きな文脈の中に位置づけられます。
MNREのデータによると、インドの太陽電池の年間製造能力は2024年3月から2025年3月の12か月間でほぼ3倍の25GWに達し、同期間にモジュール製造能力も38GWから74GWへほぼ倍増しました。
さらに
2025年11月時点ではモジュール製造能力が約144GWに到達したとMNREは報告しています。

（2）バングラデシュ：1.23億ドル基金設立

バングラデシュは、屋上太陽光発電やその他の再生可能エネルギープロジェクトへの低利融資を提供するための1億2,300万ドルの基金を設立し、Finance Divisionが発表しました。
財源は今年度の開発予算からの組み替えによるものです。
IDCOL・BIFFL・PKSFを通じて資金が配分され、ネットメータリング対応の屋上PVシステム、ソーラーホームシステム、産業用太陽光、太陽光灌漑ポンプなどの新規・拡張・更新プロジェクトが対象となっています。
同基金は「再生可能エネルギー開発政策2026〜2030」のもと、2030年までに再生可能エネルギーの発電シェアを20%にする目標を支えるものと位置づけられています。

（3）豪州：1.86GWh蓄電プロジェクト

ビクトリア州の州営電力会社SECが、400MW／1.86GWhのBaranduda蓄電プロジェクトへ最大4,300万豪ドルを出資し、15年間の供給契約でプロジェクト出力の50%を取得することが合意されました。
ビクトリア州政府はこの合意を、州と年金基金による再生可能エネルギー分野初の官民共同プロジェクトと述べています。
ただし、
建設開始は2026年11月を予定しており
、
稼働は2028年末の見込みです。
「着工確定」という表現は、投資最終決定・契約合意の事実に基づいていますが、物理的着工はまだ先であり、正確には「投資合意・契約締結」と表現するほうが適切です。

---

▍正当な懸念と誇張・誤認の分離

正当な懸念として認められる部分

インド・バングラデシュ・豪州のいずれの案件も、それぞれ一次情報で確認された実際の出来事であり、アジア太平洋地域で再生可能エネルギー投資が加速しているという全体的な文脈は事実に基づいています。
日本の太陽光エネルギー市場は2025年時点で65億ドルと評価されており、IMARC Groupはその市場が2034年までにCAGR 7.89%で成長すると予測しています。
この成長率の水準が周辺国の動向と比較して議論の対象となるのは、正当な問題意識といえます。また、制度的課題（長期の許認可プロセスや土地利用制約）が導入ペースに影響しているという指摘も、政策議論として正当な論点です。

誇張・誤認として留意が必要な部分

SNS言説における「着工確定」という表現は、事実よりも先行した表現です。豪州Barandudaプロジェクトは出資・契約合意が確認されたものの、物理的着工は2026年11月の予定です。また、インドの「2.2GW工場稼働」という言説は事実ですが、それがどの企業のどの種類の製造（セル製造であり、モジュールや発電所ではない）かという文脈が省略されることで、実態より広い印象を与える可能性があります。さらに、周辺国との単純な比較から「日本だけが停滞している」という断定的結論を導くことは、各国固有の市場段階・制度環境・エネルギーミックスの差異を無視するものであり、慎重な留保が求められます。

---

▍国際的文脈・技術トレンドとの接続

アジア太平洋地域における再生可能エネルギー投資の加速は、個別案件にとどまらない構造的変化を反映しています。インドでは国産化推進（ALMM制度）を軸としたサプライチェーン内製化が加速しており、
ALMM制度の復活が2024年の製造能力増強の主要な推進力となっており、政府支援プロジェクトを国内製品に限定することで中国製品の流入を抑制する狙いがあります。
バングラデシュでは、
LNG輸入への補助金負担が2026年4〜6月期に最大約10億7,000万ドルに達するとの試算もあり
、化石燃料依存コストの上昇が再エネ転換を後押しする構造が明確になっています。豪州では、
95%再生可能エネルギー発電という法定目標（2035年）と6.3GW以上の蓄電容量目標
を掲げており、大規模蓄電への公民連携投資はその実現手段として位置づけられています。これらは短期的な投機的投資ではなく、政策目標と紐づいた中長期的な構造変化の一部です。

---

▍4つのAIによる多角的分析を統合すると、次のように整理できます

今回の3案件は、それぞれ独立した事実でありながら、共通の構造を持っています。インドは製造能力の内製化、バングラデシュは慢性的な電力不足・外貨制約・化石燃料コストへの対応、豪州は脱石炭と系統安定化という、各国固有の政策的文脈から再エネ・蓄電投資を加速させています。いずれも「再エネが割安だから」という単一の動機ではなく、エネルギー安全保障・産業政策・系統安定という複合的な必要性から投資判断がなされています。

この複合的な動機構造は、日本にとっても示唆的です。日本では国内言説がコスト論や景観問題に集中する傾向がある一方、周辺国では「再エネを導入しないことのコスト」が政策判断の起点になっています。日本固有の制度的課題（長期の許認可プロセス、土地利用制約、系統接続の条件等）は、正当な政策論点として丁寧に扱われるべきものですが、それが「推進そのものへの否定」として機能するとき、国際的な投資競争における位置づけとの乖離が生じます。SNS上の言説はこの乖離を可視化した点で意義がある一方、各国の条件差を捨象して単純比較する構造的リスクも内包しています。4視点を統合すると、「比較対象を正確に設定し、制度論・政策論・コスト論を分離して議論する姿勢」が今後の建設的な国内言説に不可欠だという構造が見えてきます。

---

▍まとめ

先週報じられたインド・バングラデシュ・豪州の3案件はいずれも一次情報で確認された事実に基づいており、「架空の出来事」ではありません。ただし、「着工確定」等の表現には精度の留保が必要です。アジア太平洋地域の再エネ・蓄電投資加速は構造的・政策的な裏付けをもつ動きです。日本との比較を議論する際は、制度環境・市場段階・エネルギー安全保障上の文脈の差異を丁寧に踏まえた上で、建設的な政策論議に接続することが求められます。

Timex Group India beyond Q1 FY27 numbers

Timex Group India is not just about Timex watches. It has a portfolio across price points with Timex, Guess, Versace, Ferragamo, Nautica, Philipp Plein, Furla and newer brands like Aston Martin. It manufactures and assembles watches in India and sells through e-commerce, 5000+ multi-brand outlets, large format stores, its own retail network and luxury retail.

The scale up has been sharp. Revenue has moved from ₹422 Cr in FY24 to ₹540 Cr in FY25 and ₹801 Cr in FY26. More importantly, EBITDA margin expanded from 8.3% to 9.2% to 14.5% over the same period.

Q1 FY27 continued this trend with total income of ₹219 Cr, up 30%, EBITDA of ₹35.8 Cr, up 63%, EBITDA margin of 16.3% vs 13%, and PBT of ₹33.8 Cr, up 70%. Timex and Guess led brand growth, Aston Martin was among the fastest growing brands, while e-commerce and trade led channel growth.

The Baddi plant produced around 4 million watches last year and capacity has already been increased to 6 million. This gives Timex room to grow volumes without immediately adding another large manufacturing setup.

The opportunity is coming from multiple directions; growth of the core Timex brand, scaling Guess and other premium brands, adding newer brands, e-commerce and getting more sales through an already large distribution network.

One unusual development has been promoter holding falling from 74.93% to exactly 51% through two OFSs. The global parent has monetised a large part of its holding but continues to retain majority control. It has consequently also increased the public float substantially.

The gaps are mainly around disclosure. Timex does not conduct concalls, so it is difficult to get brand wise revenue, volume vs pricing growth, ASP trends, brand level margins or detailed forward guidance. Royalty and advertising costs also need to be watched.

The numbers to follow now are revenue growth and margins. If 25% to 30% sales growth continues with EBITDA margins sustaining around 15% to 16%, operating leverage can keep earnings growth well ahead of revenue growth.

🚨 IT STOCKS UNDER PRESSURE FOR 6TH STRAIGHT SESSION: NIFTY IT DOWN 4% IN 6 DAYS

Indian IT stocks extended their decline on September 25, with rising US bond yields, crude oil above $100 and concerns around global technology spending keeping the sector under pressure.

🔹 Nifty IT: down ~0.6% at 10:30 AM
🔹 6-session decline: over 4%
🔹 Infosys: down ~2%
🔹 TCS: down ~0.5%
🔹 OFSS: down ~5%
🔹 Nifty IT remained the weakest sectoral index

Only a handful of IT names, including HCLTech, LTM and Persistent Systems, were trading in positive territory during the morning session.

WHY ARE IT STOCKS FALLING? 👀

The biggest macro concern is the renewed rise in US interest-rate expectations.

Crude oil above $100 has intensified global inflation worries, while comments from US Federal Reserve policymakers have strengthened expectations that additional rate hikes may be required.

Higher US rates can potentially slow economic activity and discretionary technology spending, an important factor for Indian IT companies because of their significant exposure to the US market.

INFOSYS UNDER PRESSURE 📉

Infosys fell around 2% today after already losing roughly 5% over the previous five sessions.

The sector continues to face questions around:

🔹 Weak discretionary technology spending
🔹 Higher-for-longer US interest rates
🔹 AI-led pricing disruption
🔹 Pressure on traditional IT-services models
🔹 Near-term earnings growth

OFSS HAS AN ADDITIONAL PROBLEM ⚠️

Oracle Financial Services Software fell around 5%, making it one of the biggest losers in the broader market.

Its US parent Oracle fell more than 3% overnight after reports that it invoked force majeure relating to the massive Project Jupiter AI data-centre development in New Mexico because of potential power-related delays.

However, OFSS has separately clarified that it is a distinct listed entity and has no knowledge of developments concerning Oracle's New Mexico data-centre project.

KEY TAKEAWAY 📌

The current IT correction isn't being driven by a single factor.

Higher US rates + expensive crude + cautious global tech spending + AI disruption concerns are collectively putting pressure on sector sentiment.

The Nifty IT's six-session decline of more than 4% shows that investors are again reassessing growth expectations for Indian technology companies.

WHAT TO WATCH 👀

The upcoming September-quarter earnings season becomes particularly important.

Management commentary on discretionary spending, large-deal wins, AI-related revenue, pricing, margins and FY27 growth expectations could determine whether the current weakness remains primarily macro-driven or starts showing up materially in earnings.

For now, Indian IT remains caught between the long-term AI opportunity and the near-term risks of higher rates, slower global spending and disruption to traditional services.

FLY went and looked. Short answer: THG's mainnet footprint today is a handful of tx and under 0.1 ℏ a day. But it wasn't always, and you don't need THG to disclose wallets to find out. The chain gives them up if you read memos, metadata and account lineage instead of names.

What we found:

• BillsOnChain (THG-built, w/ String Metaverse). Treasury 0.0.10470448, six NFT collections 0.0.10471518–23 (brand is only in the token memo, which is why nobody saw it). 437,051 mints 13 May → 29 Jun, 111,787 ℏ in fees ($8,746 at network rates, exactly $0.02 a mint). On 13 June that ONE account was 62.78% of all mainnet fees. Died 29 Jun 16:03Z mid-mint with INSUFFICIENT_PAYER_BALANCE. 0 tx since.

• IDTrust: confirmed live. Payer 0.0.9243240 "Identity Provider account", writing DIDs to "Production DID Management Topic" 0.0.10773260. THG's own prod schema host serves a doc that embeds the mainnet topic, so this one's not a guess. 33,483 DIDs lifetime, 688 ℏ total. September: 39 DIDs in 24 days = 1.6/day. About a dollar a week.

• SECUTIX ticket pilot (high confidence, not confirmed: nobody's named the token). Token 0.0.10650089 "STX", 216,381 mints in 9 days bracketing Paléo Festival Nyon 21–26 Jul (210k tickets sold). ~229.5k ℏ burned, the biggest single-operator fee spend we found on Hedera this year, ~¾ of network fees that week. Then stopped.

• IBM, PwC, Merck, CONFED/EcoGuard, Teleport, BEEAH: not found. Not found ≠ zero, but read the releases: catalog listing, PoC, pilot. Those don't put tx on mainnet.

Two corrections to the method, @itsbrandond, with love:

1. Since HIP-1259 (19 Feb 2026) fees don't go to nodes / 0.0.98 / 0.0.800 / 0.0.801 per transaction any more. Every fee lands in 0.0.802 and gets swept once a day at 00:00 UTC. So "look at HBAR sent to the node, treasury and staking wallets" returns nothing after Feb, and the node/treasury/staking split in the hgraph methodology is stale. Revenue per payer = Σ charged_tx_fee. Network total = one query on 0.0.802's daily sweep (median 6,883 ℏ/day lately).
2. hgraph's per-payer fee function credits EVM tx fees to the relay, not the account actually debited. Watch for that if you lean on it.

So: two big bursts that together were ~1/6 of every fee the network has charged since Feb, then quiet. Enterprise usage on Hedera is real, bursty, partner-funded, and stops when the top-ups stop.

All of it checkable on the public mirror node with the IDs above. Full write-up with every query to follow. Building it into #Flyterm as revenue so nobody has to do this by hand again. 🪰

Hermione Granger may have been naturally talented, but her real strength came from how determined she was to learn everything she possibly could. From her earliest days at Hogwarts, she stood out because of her intelligence, preparation, and ability to think quickly when things went wrong. She regularly mastered spells and concepts that were difficult for students her age. Whether she was brewing complicated potions, learning advanced charms, or figuring out mysteries everyone else had overlooked, Hermione rarely stopped until she found an answer.

But Hermione’s abilities went far beyond earning good grades. Again and again, she used what she had learned to protect Harry and Ron when their lives were in danger. During the Horcrux hunt, her protective enchantments and careful planning became essential to keeping the trio alive. She was capable of nonverbal magic and performed complicated spells such as the Undetectable Extension Charm and Protean Charm. She even made the heartbreaking decision to alter her parents’ memories in an effort to protect them from Voldemort and his followers.

Even when Hermione was surrounded by witches and wizards with far more experience, she proved that she could hold her own. Her motivation was never about becoming famous or being considered the most powerful witch in the room. She wanted to use her abilities to help others and fight for what she believed was right. Her knowledge of magical history, laws, spells, and theory repeatedly gave Harry and Ron information they desperately needed. Sometimes Hermione’s greatest contribution wasn’t a spell at all—it was simply knowing something nobody else did.

Hermione’s story ultimately shows that magical talent alone only gets someone so far. Her intelligence became extraordinary because she combined it with relentless studying, bravery, compassion, and determination. She never stopped asking questions or trying to understand more about the world around her. Hermione Granger proved that knowledge could be every bit as powerful as magic itself.

🚨 OFSS FALLS OVER 5%: ORACLE TRIGGERS 'FORCE MAJEURE' ON MASSIVE AI DATA CENTRE PROJECT

Oracle Financial Services Software (OFSS) shares came under heavy pressure again after its US parent Oracle issued a force majeure notice linked to Project Jupiter, a massive AI data-centre campus in New Mexico.

🔹 OFSS intraday fall: over 5%
🔹 Intraday low: ₹10,332
🔹 Lowest level in over 9 weeks
🔹 Trading volumes jumped sharply
🔹 Oracle shares also fell in the US
🔹 Project Jupiter targeted to come online in 2028

WHAT HAPPENED? 👀

Oracle issued a force majeure notice to a Blue Owl unit developing Project Jupiter, citing potential delays in securing adequate power for the facility.

The notice does not mean Oracle is exiting the project.

According to reports, Oracle is seeking contractual protection that could allow it to delay certain payments if the data centre is delayed and fails to become operational on schedule.

POWER IS THE BIG ISSUE ⚡

Project Jupiter is designed to handle around 2.45 GW of capacity, making reliable energy infrastructure critical.

A natural-gas pipeline intended to support the site has reportedly been delayed by nearly six months, while other permitting issues around the project's power infrastructure remain unresolved.

The project is part of the massive AI infrastructure build-out associated with Oracle and OpenAI.

KEY TAKEAWAY 📌

The development highlights one of the biggest challenges emerging from the global AI boom:

AI demand may be enormous, but building enough data centres, power generation and grid infrastructure fast enough is becoming increasingly difficult.

However, an important distinction is necessary for OFSS investors.

OFSS has previously clarified to the exchanges that it is a separate listed entity from Oracle and said it has no knowledge of developments concerning Oracle's New Mexico data-centre project.

Therefore, the current OFSS price reaction is primarily linked to sentiment around its parent Oracle rather than a disclosed operational impact on OFSS itself.

WHAT TO WATCH 👀

Oracle has said Project Jupiter remains on schedule and that it remains fully committed to the New Mexico project. Blue Owl has also said the notice does not change the parties' financial commitments.

The key monitorables are now power availability, permits, the 2028 commissioning timeline and any changes to financing or contractual obligations.

For OFSS specifically, the crucial question is whether parent-level AI infrastructure concerns remain only a sentiment overhang or eventually have any measurable impact on the Indian listed company's fundamentals.

Update on Ramkrishna Forgings' promoter warrant infusion — turns out it's bigger than what we'd previously talked, and there's a governance item worth flagging alongside it.

We'd cited a ₹204.75 Cr promoter warrant programme (9,75,000 warrants at ₹2,100, via Riddhi Portfolio) as a confidence signal in the FY25 audit-discrepancy episode. That one's now fully converted — ₹100.80 Cr in March, ₹52.76 Cr in June, cash fully in. 

What's new: a second, separate warrant programme — 34,00,000 warrants at ₹588 (₹199.92 Cr), allotted to Chaitanya Jalan personally — has also now completed its 75% conversion tranche. Combined, promoters have actually put in ~₹404.67 Cr, not ₹204.75 Cr — roughly double the confidence signal we'd captured, and it's cash-in-hand now, not a pending commitment.

Worth flagging alongside it, not as a red flag but as a watch item: five days before this allotment, shareholders approved reclassifying MAA Chandi Financial Advisory Services — a promoter-group entity holding 3.57% of equity — from Promoter Group to Public category. A real reduction in formal promoter-group holding, happening right alongside a capital infusion increasing it elsewhere. Often this kind of reclassification is just family/trust restructuring with no change in economic control — but it's exactly the sort of promoter-structure change worth tracking rather than ignoring, especially on a name already carrying a live governance overhang from FY25.

AI is turning computing into a massive infrastructure business.

• Global data-centre investments could reach $250 billion over the next 5 years.

• India’s operational data-centre capacity is estimated to reach ~2 GW by 2028.

• Major groups like Tata, Adani, Bharti Airtel, Reliance and L&T are expanding their presence.

• New entrants are also coming in, attracted by the long-term growth in cloud, AI and digital workloads.
But the interesting part is not just the data centre itself.

• AI workloads require enormous amounts of electricity, reliable power and cooling.

• Data-centre operators are therefore increasingly looking at renewable power and long-term energy arrangements.

• High-density GPU deployments can dramatically increase power consumption per rack.

• This creates a much larger opportunity across the ecosystem -  power generation, transmission, electrical equipment, cooling systems, construction, real estate and digital infrastructure.

• In other words, the AI capex cycle could create demand far beyond semiconductor and software companies.

The next few years could therefore see a completely different infrastructure buildout in India.

• More cloud creates demand for more servers
• More AI → higher computing intensity
• Higher computing intensity → more electricity
• More electricity demand → more generation & transmission capacity
• More data centres → more cooling, electrical and construction requirements

The companies that benefit may not necessarily be the ones everyone is talking about today. The picks-and-shovels around the AI infrastructure buildout could become an equally interesting part of the story.

💥 Hidden debt and off-balance-sheet entities destroyed investor confidence.

3️⃣ Lehman Brothers — ~90%+  
📍 Sept 2008  
💥 The collapse became a defining event of the Global Financial Crisis.

4️⃣ Adani Enterprises — ~45%–50%  
📍 Jan–Feb 2023  
💥 A short-seller report triggered a massive sell-off across the group.

💥 Governance concerns and asset-quality fears led to institutional exits.

Treatment of the possible large tax bill among the outstanding issues that could affect the deal

Two sides targeting a binding agreement by December

VW has spent nearly two years looking for a local partner in India to share costs and risks — after talks with Mahindra & Mahindra broke down

German automaker aims to crack India's vast, fast-growing car market

Holds only a token share through its Skoda Auto unit despite substantial investment in local manufacturing and development of dedicated models over past two decades

The Tax Issue
Stems from Indian government's allegation that VW misclassified some vehicle assembly kits imported from Germany, Czech Republic and Hungary between 2012 and 2024

Misclassification allegedly reduced the levies VW had to pay — a claim VW has denied

VW challenging the tax demand before a court in Mumbai

NUSI CONGRATULATES CAPT. B. K. TYAGI

Heartiest Congratulations to Capt. B. K. Tyagi on being elected President of the Indian National Shipowners’ Association (INSA) for 2026–27

On behalf of the National Union of Seafarers of India (NUSI) and the Indian seafaring community, I extend our warmest congratulations to Capt. B. K. Tyagi, Chairman & Managing Director, Shipping Corporation of India (SCI), on his election as President of the Indian National Shipowners’ Association (INSA) for the term 2026–27.

NUSI shares a long-standing association with the Shipping Corporation of India, built over decades of engagement on matters concerning Indian shipping and, most importantly, the men and women who serve at sea.

Capt. Tyagi’s journey from joining SCI as a Trainee Nautical Officer Cadet to becoming a Master Mariner and eventually leading SCI as its Chairman & Managing Director gives him a deep understanding of both life at sea and the responsibilities of maritime leadership. 

At a time when Indian shipping is entering an important phase of growth and transformation, strong cooperation between shipowners, seafarers, maritime unions and the Government will be essential. We look forward to continuing our constructive engagement with INSA under Capt. Tyagi’s leadership, particularly in advancing seafarer employment, training and future skills, safety, welfare, social security and decent working conditions.

When Indian shipping grows, Indian seafarers must grow with it.

NUSI wishes Capt. B. K. Tyagi every success in his new responsibility and looks forward to working together towards a stronger Indian shipping industry and a secure, skilled and respected Indian seafaring community.

Congratulations, Capt. B. K. Tyagi!

Milind Kandalgaonkar
General Secretary-cum-Treasurer
National Union of Seafarers of India (NUSI)
On behalf of NUSI and the Indian seafaring community

1.​🧵 Thread: The #Polysilicon Race, India's Push for Self-Reliance & The Mining Ecosystem

​1/7: What is Polysilicon? 🧪

​Polysilicon (Polycrystalline Silicon) is a hyper-purified form of silicon. It is the fundamental building block of the modern digital and clean-energy world.
​Without polysilicon, there are no solar panels and no microchips.

​2/7: Key Uses of Polysilicon ⚡💻
​• Solar PV Energy (~90% of global demand): Polysilicon chunks are melted down to cast single-crystal ingots, sliced into wafer-thin sheets, and processed into solar cells.
​• Semiconductors: Refined to extreme "Electronic Grade" purity (99.9999999% pure) to make silicon wafers for CPUs, memory chips (DRAM/NAND), and microcontrollers.
​• Electronics & Displays: Used to manufacture Thin-Film Transistors (TFTs) in OLED/LCD screens and micro-sensors (MEMS).

​3/7: Who Manufactures Polysilicon in India? 🇮🇳
​Currently, India has zero active commercial production of polysilicon, leaving the country dependent on imports (primarily from China, the US, and Europe).
​However, two massive Indian conglomerates are changing this through fully integrated "Quartz-to-Module" giga-complexes:
​Reliance Industries Ltd ($RELIANCE): Building a full polysilicon and ingot-wafer integration at the Dhirubhai Ambani Green Energy Giga Complex in Jamnagar, Gujarat.
​Adani Enterprises Ltd ($ADANIENT): Developing a 30,000 MTPA integrated polysilicon plant at Mundra, Gujarat.

​4/7: The Raw Material Chain: From Quartz to Polysilicon 🪨
​Polysilicon isn't mined directly—it is manufactured from high-purity quartz through a multi-step refinement process:
​High-Purity Quartz (SiO2) ➔ Metallurgical-Grade Silicon ➔ Solar/Electronic Grade Polysilicon
​• High-purity quartz (SiO2) is smelted with carbon to produce Metallurgical Silicon (~98% pure).
• MGS is chemically refined (via the Siemens or FBR process) to achieve solar or electronic grade purity.

​5/7: Listed Mining & Mineral Companies in India ⛏️
​Companies tied to the upstream raw materials required for silicon and refractories include:
​• GMDC ($GMDCLTD): State-owned mining giant in Gujarat holding vast reserves of silica sand and quartz near the Jamnagar & Mundra giga-factories.
​• Owais Metal & Mineral ($OWAIS): Sourcing and processing high-grade industrial quartz lumps and silica sand.
​• 20 Microns ($20MICRONS): Advanced industrial minerals producer specializing in processed high-purity silica powder.
​• Maithan Alloys ($MAITHANALL): Processes quartz into silicon alloys and metallurgical-grade silicon precursors.

​6/7: Key Enablers: High-Purity Silicon Carbide & Tools ⚙️
​Beyond raw quartz, polysilicon manufacturing requires specialized ceramics and cutting tools:
​• Carborundum Universal ($CARBORUNIV): Produces ultra-high-purity Silicon Carbide (CUMI Krysta®) and heavy-duty refractories used in reactors and furnaces to grow single-crystal silicon ingots.
​• Wendt India ($WENDT): Manufactures specialized diamond cutting tools and precision machine tools used to slice silicon ingots into wafers with micro-inch tolerances.

​7/7: The Bottom Line 📉➡️📈
​India's ambition to become a global solar and semiconductor manufacturing hub depends on securing domestic polysilicon production.
​The transition from 100% import dependency to domestic "Quartz-to-Solar" capability makes the entire supply chain—from quartz miners to advanced ceramic makers and mega-conglomerates—a key industrial sector to monitor over the coming years.

Imagine travelling from Kurseong to Darjeeling in just 45 minutes instead of 4–6 hours by road during peak tourist season. 🏔️🚡

That is the vision behind a proposed ₹3,000 crore ropeway project that could transform connectivity, tourism and the movement of essential goods across the Darjeeling hills.

📍KURSEONG–DARJEELING ROPEWAY
🚡 Aerial length: Approximately 20–22 km
⏱️ Proposed travel time: Around 45 minutes
💰 Estimated investment: ₹3,000 crore
🏗️ Implementation model: BOOT (Build–Own–Operate–Transfer)
🚉 Four or five stations, including intermediate stops
📦 Potential dual use: Passenger transport during the day and movement of essential supplies at night

The project is intended to provide an alternative to the congested NH-110 (Hill Cart Road), where journeys can take several hours during peak tourist periods.

Building another road through the steep, landslide-prone terrain presents significant challenges. A ropeway could offer a faster and potentially more scenic transport option while reducing pressure on the existing road network.

The feasibility study has reportedly been completed and considered viable. The government is expected to invite private companies through an Expression of Interest (EOI) under the BOOT model.

🤔 COULD ADANI BE INTERESTED?
On 24 September, Gautam Adani announced that the Adani Group plans to invest over ₹1 lakh crore in West Bengal by 2035, with roads, bridges and ropeways among the identified sectors.

Adani Enterprises is also involved in the 12.9 km Sonprayag–Kedarnath ropeway project, reportedly valued at ₹4,081 crore under the Centre’s Parvatmala programme.

🏔️ THE BIGGER PICTURE
If implemented successfully, the Kurseong–Darjeeling ropeway could become more than a tourist attraction. It could form part of a wider strategy to improve hill connectivity, reduce road congestion and strengthen the tourism economy.

The government has also discussed other potential ropeway links in the region, including routes around Darjeeling and Kalimpong.

Could this become one of Bengal’s most transformative hill infrastructure projects? 🚡

My Thoughts on Ramkrishna Forgings Ltd

Management is targeting Rs 8,000 Cr revenue by FY29, versus 4,238 Cr in FY26 - implying roughly 24% revenue CAGR over the next three years.  

If the company can get back to its historical 20–22% EBITDA margins, 8,000 Cr revenue could translate into roughly Rs 1,600–1,760 Cr EBITDA. 

For me, the next 2–3 years are essentially a revenue growth + margin recovery story.  The opportunity looks interesting, but the key things to track will be execution, capacity ramp-up, incremental margins, capex and balance-sheet strength.  

The 8,000 Cr target is ambitious, but if execution remains on track and margins normalize, the earnings potential could look quite different by FY29.

The global auto landscape is undergoing a massive realignment.

Chinese EV makers are dismantling Europe’s home turf, and legacy Western giants are scrambling for cover in India.

Here’s how the battlefield is shifting:

1. Europe’s Fortress is Cracking
BYD, MG, and Chery are outpricing European OEMs on their own soil. Even with EU tariffs, a 25–30% Chinese cost advantage, vertical battery control, and software-first cockpits are driving German margins into the red and triggering plant shutdown warnings.

2. The India Trade Dynamic: Europe vs. China
• India–EU FTA push: Europe wants steep cuts on imported car duties (CBUs/CKDs). India’s response? Phased cuts tied to local manufacturing commitments ($500M+ capex, ~50% domestic value addition).
• The China reality: No FTA on the table. With Press Note 3 restricting direct FDI, Chinese EV tech can enter India mainly through local JVs and alliances (e.g., JSW–MG).

3. Home Turf Defense
Tata Motors and Mahindra & Mahindra aren't blinking. They own the mass-to-mid EV space with localized supply chains, dealer dominance, and aggressive price points. European brands sit at barely ~2% Indian market share; they can't survive on imported models.

4. The Volkswagen Playbook & The JSW Stumbling Block
VW needs an Indian giant to build affordable platforms and split capital costs. It signed a non-binding MoU with JSW for a 51:49 JV, with a binding deal targeted by year-end.
The catch? A disputed ~$1.4B (₹11,526 Cr) customs notice hanging over VW/Skoda for allegedly classifying imported kits as parts instead of CKDs. JSW has drawn a hard line: VW must ring-fence and absorb the entire tax liability before any binding deal is signed.

The Bottom Line:
The road to surviving the EV transition runs straight through deep localization, not import duty workarounds. If legacy giants can't crack local alliances in markets like India, they risk getting squeezed from both ends.

【先週のSNSでのエネルギー 2026/09/25】

インホイールモーター技術をめぐる言説の現在地：「実用化困難」論の妥当な核心と、情報更新の遅延がもたらす過剰な悲観論

---

▍このトピックが注目された背景

EV（電気自動車）をめぐる技術論争の一環として、インホイールモーター（以下IWM）の「実用化困難」論が日本語SNSで定期的に浮上してきました。その背景には、
「これまでコンセプト車で盛んに用いられてきたインホイールモーターの社会実装が近づきつつある」と日経クロステック（2025年4月）が報じる
など、国内外で開発ニュースが相次いでいる状況があります。一方で日本語言説圏では依然として「実用化は困難」「量販化の見通しはない」という論調が根強く、その認識と実際の開発状況との間に乖離が生じていることが、改めて議論の焦点となっています。

---

▍言説の構造と広がり

日本語SNS上で「実用化困難」論が広がりやすい理由は、技術課題の「実在性」と「過去の議論の蓄積」の二つにあります。

「インホイールモーターは以前から存在しますが、特に低速走行時や平坦な道路では実用化しやすい技術です。一方で、悪路ではモーターがホイール内部にあるため、ばね下重量が増え、路面の凹凸への追従性が低下しやすいという課題があります」
という解説が繰り返し参照されており、これはSNS上で「実用化困難論」の説得力ある論拠として機能しています。

加えて、
「インホイールモーターは100年以上前に実用化されたが、それ以降は現代まで市販化はほぼされていない」
という歴史的文脈が組み合わされることで、「かつても今もダメな技術」という認識フレームが固定されやすい構造があります。技術課題を示す言説は具体的・直感的にわかりやすく、反論側の「開発が進んでいる」という情報は一次情報へのアクセスが必要なため、拡散力に非対称性が生じます。日本固有のEV受容フレーム（内燃機関技術への信頼感・慎重な評価傾向）も、この非対称性を強化する背景として作用していると考えられます。

---

▍データ・事実による検証

確認できた一次情報に基づき、以下を記述します。

国内の開発状況： 
開発グループには日立製作所のほか、Astemo（アステモ）、日立インダストリアルプロダクツ、大同特殊鋼、東北特殊鋼の5社が参加し、開発資金の一部にNEDO「グリーンイノベーション基金」を活用している。
Astemoは軽自動車に搭載可能な12インチサイズの空冷ダイレクト駆動システムを2025年5月の展示会に出展し、これまでに開発した16インチ・19インチに加えて、2030年ごろの実用化を目指す方針を示した。
また
AstemoはEV用インホイールモーターで、内部のコイルを容易に取り出せる製品を開発しており、銅の回収率が高まることで欧州の環境規制にも対応する。

国際的な動向： 
BMWスタートアップガレージとミュンヘン拠点のDeepDriveが路上試験（ロードテスト）を実施している。
DeepDriveは世界最大手自動車メーカー10社のうち8社と協働していると自社発表している。
なお、この数値はDeepDrive自身の表明によるもので、第三者による検証は本稿では確認できていない。
同社のモーターは磁性材料を約50%、鉄を約80%削減したとされ、SiC-MOSFETインバーターと組み合わせたシステム効率は98%超とDeepDriveは説明している。

生産車への採用： 
ルノーグループはProtean Electricをルノー5 Turbo 3EのIWMサプライヤーとして確定しており、欧州初のIWM搭載量産乗用車になると両社は発表した。
生産台数は1,980台に限定され、2027年からの納車開始が確認されている。
ただし、これはハイパフォーマンス車の限定生産であり、大量生産・汎用量販車への採用とは明確に区別する必要があります。

---

▍正当な懸念と誇張・誤認の分離

正当な懸念：

バネ下重量の増加・熱管理の困難・システム統合の複雑さは、現在も業界内で公認された技術課題です。
「このばね下荷重の増加という技術課題の克服が不可欠」
であるという認識は、現時点でも妥当な懸念として維持されています。「大手自動車メーカーによる汎用量販EVへの大規模採用」がいまだ実現していないことも事実であり、この点での「困難」の指摘は証拠と整合しています。

誇張・誤認として整理できる部分：

一方、「実用化は不可能・停滞している」という断定的な論調は、現時点の状況とずれがあります。
日経クロステックは「社会実装が近づきつつある」と報じており
、欧州ではIWM搭載の量産乗用車の納車が計画されています。また、日本語言説圏で流通する「困難論」の多くが2020年以前の議論を参照しており、2024〜2025年以降に具体化した路上試験・限定量産・OEMサプライヤー契約といった進展が反映されていない傾向が観察されます。「技術課題が残る」と「実用化は困難・不可能」の間には論理的な飛躍があり、この混同が過剰な悲観論を形成しています。

---

▍国際的文脈・技術トレンドとの接続

Protean Electricとルノーは、ルノー5 Turbo 3Eが「欧州初のIWM搭載量産乗用車になる」と表明しています。
さらに
この量産プログラムへの技術統合の詳細は、2026年ウィーン国際モーターシンポジウムで発表される予定であり、熱管理・シャシー統合・制御系といった、従来IWM普及の障壁とされてきた課題への対応が初めて工学的に詳述されることが見込まれている。

また、
IWMは省スペース・高効率・軽量・低コストが実現すれば幅広い車種に適用でき、高いスケーラビリティが期待できる
と指摘されており、中長期的に見れば特定用途・車種から順次展開されていく可能性を示す情報が集積しています。日本の開発体制も国際的な流れから孤立しているわけではなく、NEDOを通じた産学連携が2030年を目標に継続している点は重要です。

---

▍4つのAIによる多角的分析を統合すると、次のように整理できます

事実検証・政策社会文脈・国際技術トレンド・言説拡散メカニズムの4視点を統合すると、日本語言説圏における「実用化困難」論は、技術課題の実在を核心に持ちながら、情報更新の遅延によって誇張された形で流通しているという構造が見えてきます。

バネ下重量・熱管理・統合複雑性という課題は現在も有効ですが、それらは「不可能の証拠」ではなく「解決途上の課題」として位置付けるのが証拠に照らした適切な認識です。国際的には既に路上試験・限定生産・OEM供給契約という段階に到達しており、「実験室の夢物語」という言説フレームはすでに現実と乖離しています。

また、政策の観点からは、日本国内での情報更新スピードの遅さが、技術受容における判断の質を低下させるリスクとして浮かび上がります。科学的根拠に基づく冷静な段階評価—「課題あり・移行期にある」—こそが、技術政策・投資判断・消費者理解を支える基盤となります。「実用化困難」を強調する言説と「万能技術」として過大評価する言説の両極を避け、現在の開発段階を正確に記述することが求められています。

---

▍まとめ

インホイールモーター技術は、バネ下重量・熱管理・システム統合という実在する課題を抱えながらも、路上試験・限定量産・OEM契約という形で「移行期」にあります。日本語言説圏で根強い「実用化困難」論は技術課題の存在という点で部分的に妥当ですが、2024〜2025年以降の国際的な進展を反映しきれておらず、過去の議論の反復にとどまる部分が混在しています。技術言説の精度向上には、「困難」と「不可能」の論理的な区別が不可欠です。

---

One way I look at the railway space is: don’t just buy the RAILWAY CAPEX narrative - identify who has the capability to actually capture the earnings.

Titagarh Rail Systems stands out to me among the wagon/rolling-stock names because the story is no longer only about wagons. 

Its passenger-rail business is becoming increasingly meaningful, with 1,280 Vande Bharat coaches and 441 metro coaches in the order book in FY26, alongside a large freight wagon franchise. 

Its BHEL partnership also gives it exposure to the 80-trainset Vande Bharat programme + 35-year maintenance opportunity.

The company is also building capabilities across stainless steel, aluminium, propulsion and other rail subsystems.  

Then there are Cosmic CRF and Airfloa Rail Technology, which are much smaller and therefore come with a completely different risk profile. 

Cosmic CRF is a focused manufacturer of cold-rolled formed steel sections and engineered components for railways and infrastructure; its order visibility has reportedly increased to around ₹760 crore, while recent orders include supplies to railway wagon manufacturers and Indian Railways. 

Airfloa is more of a railway components and turnkey interiors play, with exposure to LHB, Amrit Bharat, Vande Bharat, metro and RRTS projects. Its FY26 revenue reached about ₹320 crore, while the company has reported an order book above ₹465 crore. 

Facts are one thing. Narrative is another. 

Media can spoon-feed you a story about an entire sector, but ultimately earnings have to validate it. 

I would rather look 3–5 years ahead at order-book quality, execution capacity, margin potential, competitive positioning and earnings visibility. 

Long-term investing doesn't mean buy and forget. The world is changing faster, and the companies we own need to keep evolving with it.

Titagarh, Cosmic CRF and Airfloa are three very different risk-reward profiles within the same broader railway opportunity. 

No recommendation. DYODD.

Indian Railways’ coach upgrade cycle could create a multi-year opportunity for the railway manufacturing ecosystem.

With around 1,600 mail/express rakes targeted for conversion to LHB coaches by FY28, and further movement towards Amrit Bharat push-pull trains, the opportunity is not limited to complete coach manufacturers. 

The fleet modernisation will require a wide range of components - bogies, wheelsets, axles, doors, seats, electrical systems and other equipment.

Some names worth tracking across this ecosystem include Titagarh Rail Systems, BEML, Jupiter Wagons and Ramkrishna Forgings, among others.

The bigger opportunity could be the entire railway value chain as Railways continues replacing older ICF coaches and upgrading passenger trains.

The key now is to track order inflows, execution capacity and margins  because a large capex opportunity doesn't automatically translate into equal shareholder value for every company.

Raw material choice decides the process, the price, the customer, and the demand cycle for any pipe.

Plastic / polymer pipes
Made from PVC, CPVC and similar resins. Used in agriculture, bathroom plumbing and sub-soil water lines.  
Key players: Supreme Industries, Astral, Finolex, Prince, Apollo Pipes, Ashirvad, Prakash Pipes.

Stainless steel pipes
Steel alloyed with nickel and chromium for corrosion resistance. Used in food processing, dairy, pharma, chemicals and railings. Higher cost, so specified only where ordinary steel would rust and fail.

Carbon steel pipes
Made from ordinary steel. This is the largest category.

Carbon steel pipes split into three types by manufacturing process:

Ductile Iron (DI) pipes — cast from pig iron. Main use: drinking-water pipelines under Jal Jeevan Mission. Players: Rashmi Group, Jindal SAW, Electrosteel, Jai Balaji.

Seamless pipes — no welded joint, so they handle very high pressure. Used in oil & gas drilling, boilers and defence. Players: Maharashtra Seamless, ISMT, Jindal SAW, Ratnamani.

Welded pipes — a flat steel coil is rolled into a tube and the seam is welded. This is the biggest segment. It further divides into large-diameter LSAW/HSAW pipes (oil & gas trunk lines) and ERW pipes (Electric Resistance Welded), the most common type for general use.
Players: APL Apollo, Tata Tubes, Welspun (ERW line), Sambhav Steel Tubes, etc

Large-diameter LSAW/HSAW players: Man Industries (India) Ltd, Welspun Corp, Jindal SAW.

Rain Industries Limited (Rain Carbon) has entered into a strategic collaboration with BioBTX BV, a circular chemistry technology developer. 🤝 This partnership aims to bring renewable aromatic products to the chemical industry, fostering more circular and sustainable value chains. ♻️

𝗞𝗲𝘆 𝗛𝗶𝗴𝗵𝗹𝗶𝗴𝗵𝘁𝘀:

- 𝗖𝗼𝗹𝗹𝗮𝗯𝗼𝗿𝗮𝘁𝗶𝗼𝗻 𝗙𝗼𝗰𝘂𝘀: BioBTX will convert plastic waste into renewable aromatic oil using its proprietary Integrated Catalytic Cracking Process (ICCP) technology. Rain Carbon will then process this oil into benzene, phthalic anhydride, and other aromatic derivatives.
- 𝗠𝗮𝗿𝗸𝗲𝘁 𝗜𝗺𝗽𝗮𝗰𝘁: These renewable products will meet the same quality standards as conventional fossil-based products, enabling customers across various industries (e.g., pharmaceuticals, coatings, automotive) to reduce their supply chain carbon footprint without compromising performance. 📉
- 𝗕𝗶𝗼𝗕𝗧𝗫'𝘀 𝗙𝗶𝗿𝘀𝘁 𝗣𝗹𝗮𝗻𝘁: BioBTX is constructing its first commercial-scale plant in Delfzijl, the Netherlands, which is expected to be operational in early 2028. This facility will convert approximately 10,000 tonnes of plastic waste per year into renewable aromatic oil. 🏭
- 𝗦𝘁𝗿𝗮𝘁𝗲𝗴𝗶𝗰 𝗔𝗹𝗶𝗴𝗻𝗺𝗲𝗻𝘁: This collaboration aligns with Rain Carbon's mission to create value from alternative carbon sources and support the transition to a circular economy. 🌍

Kris Vanherbergen, EVP Carbon Distillation & Advanced Materials at Rain Carbon, stated that the partnership offers renewable, drop-in solutions for a sustainable future. Ton Vries, CEO of BioBTX, highlighted significant market interest in their renewable aromatic oil due to growing demand for products with higher recycled content and lower carbon footprints. 📈

Research Note: #PBFintechLimited (#Policybazaar)

1. Company Overview
PB Fintech Ltd (NSE: #POLICYBZR ) is India’s largest online insurance and credit marketplace. Its flagship platforms are:
- #Policybazaar – Insurance comparison & distribution (core business)
- #Paisabazaar ** – Credit marketplace (personal loans, credit cards, etc.)
- #PBPartners – Tech-enabled network of independent agents/advisors (offline reach into Bharat)
- Newer verticals: Corporate insurance, Reinsurance broking, PB UAE, Pensionbazaar, PB Wheels, Account Aggregator (PB Money)

Mission: Help the Indian middle class deal with Death, Disease and Disability (the 3Ds).

As of June 2026:
- 158.9 million registered consumers
- 28.1 million transacting consumers
- 71.6 million policies sold till date

2. Business Model & Unit Economics
Revenue Streams:
- Commissions / brokerage from insurers on new business
- High-margin renewal / trail income (sticky, ~80% margins)
- Credit marketplace fees
- New initiatives (PB Partners, Corporate, UAE, etc.)

Key Strengths:
- Dominant online market share (>90% of online insurance policies sold historically)
- Strong shift toward **protection products** (Health + Term) — now >70% of core online revenue
- Renewal ARR has compounded strongly (₹935 Cr in FY26, ~80% margins)
- Asset-light model with high operating leverage once scale is achieved

3. Financial Performance Snapshot
 Full Year (April 2025 – March 2026)
The company made ₹6,794 crore in total revenue. This is 37% higher than the previous year.
Insurance business grew strongly — total premium collected reached ₹29,934 crore (up 42%).
Profit almost doubled to ₹670 crore.
The company is now clearly profitable and margins are improving.

Latest Quarter (April – June 2026)
Revenue: ₹1,888 crore (up 40% from the same quarter last year).
Insurance premium: ₹8,372 crore (up 41%).
Profit: ₹163 crore (almost double compared to last year).
Profit margin improved from 6% to 9%.

Highlights:
- Profitability turned consistently positive from FY24 onwards.
- Management is on track for ~₹1,000 Cr PAT in FY27.
- Contribution margins in core online business remain healthy (~42–44%).
- Loan disbursals (Paisabazaar) also growing well (₹30,740 Cr in FY26; +33% in Q1 FY27 core online).

4. Segment Insights

#Policybazaar (Core Online):
- Health insurance market share of 
fresh retail business has risen sharply to ~18–20% (from ~4.5% in FY22).
- Protection products driving quality growth.
- Renewal income is the compounding engine.

PB Partners:
- Expanding rapidly into Tier 2–5 cities via 450k+ partners.
- Market share gains visible; lead over next player widening.

#Paisabazaar :
- Recovering and turning EBITDA positive.
- Expanding into mutual funds & bonds.

International (UAE):
- Became profitable in FY26; premium growth strong (~54% YoY).

5. Competitive Landscape
#Policybazaar remains the clear leader in digital insurance distribution in India. Key competitors include:
- InsuranceDekho (post RenewBuy merger — stronger challenger)
- Turtlemint
- Coverfox / others

Digital still forms a small portion of overall Indian insurance distribution (traditional agency + bancassurance dominate). This leaves significant runway if digital penetration rises.

6. Growth Drivers
1. Under-penetration of insurance in India (especially protection products).
2. Rising health insurance awareness + GST benefits earlier.
3. Shift from pure comparison to full-stack “phygital” (digital + offline partners).
4. High-margin renewals compounding.
5. Credit marketplace recovery + cross-sell.
6. New initiatives (Corporate, Reinsurance, UAE, Pension, etc.) providing optionality.

Management guidance: Sustain ~30% premium growth trajectory.

🚨 INSURANCE STOCKS ARE FALLING 🚨

“ HERE’S WHAT JUST HAPPENED” 

If you saw Policybazaar, insurers, banks & NBFC stocks falling today, this is the simple reason 👇

IRDAI has proposed a major change in how insurance is sold and how much distributors can earn.

⚠️ Important: These are proposals, NOT final rules yet.
Comments are open until 25 October 2026, with implementation expected from FY28 through a phased approach.

🧵 WHAT IS IRDAI TRYING TO CHANGE?

Think of it like this:

Today, insurance distributors can earn significant commissions for selling policies.

IRDAI is basically saying:

“Insurance should be sold because customers need it, not simply because the distributor earns a lot by pushing it.”

The regulator wants to reduce excessive commissions, improve transparency and make insurance more affordable and sustainable.

💰 1. LOWER EXPENSE LIMITS

IRDAI is proposing tighter limits on how much insurers can spend.

For life insurers:

➡️ Around 15% of gross direct premium in 2 years

➡️ Around 12.5% in 5 years

➡️ Some already-efficient insurers could move toward 10%

For general insurers:

➡️ Around 20% in 5 years

In simple words:

Insurers may have less room to spend heavily on commissions, distribution and other expenses.

💸 2. COMMISSIONS COULD COME DOWN

This is the part the market is worried about most.

IRDAI wants to bring back product- and channel-specific commission limits.

Instead of paying a huge amount upfront for selling a policy, payouts could be:

➡️ Lower in the first year

➡️ Spread across the policy period

➡️ More closely linked to the actual effort/service involved

This could particularly affect:

🔹 Term insurance
🔹 Health insurance
🔹 Motor insurance
🔹 Credit-linked insurance

🏦 3. BIG CHANGE FOR BANKS & NBFCs

One proposal could have a major impact:

Banks/NBFCs would not be allowed to compulsorily bundle insurance with loans.

For example:

You take a ₹50 lakh loan.

The bank cannot effectively say:

“Take this insurance policy along with the loan.”

And credit-linked insurance commissions could become as low as 2–5% in some cases.

That is potentially a big change from the economics of these products today.

🚨 4. MIS-SELLING WILL GET MORE EXPENSIVE

IRDAI also wants:

✅ Stronger anti-mis-selling rules
✅ Commission clawbacks
✅ More disclosure of commissions on large policies
✅ Restrictions on “dark patterns”
✅ Less volume-based pressure on bank employees
✅ Simpler distributor categories

The broad idea:

Sell the right insurance to the customer, not simply the product that pays the most commission.

📉 SO WHY DID INSURANCE STOCKS FALL?

Because the market immediately started calculating:

“If commissions fall → distributor income falls → earnings could fall.”

🔴 Insurance distributors

Stocks such as PB Fintech (Policybazaar) and Turtlemint were among the more heavily impacted.

Their business models are closely connected to insurance distribution economics.

Some analysts estimated that even a 10% reduction in commissions could have a meaningful impact on earnings, depending on the company’s product mix.

🔴 Insurance companies

Several life and general insurers also fell, including names such as:

HDFC Life
ICICI Prudential Life
Max Financial
SBI Life
Star Health
ICICI Lombard
LIC

Why?

Because lower expense limits + lower upfront commissions could affect:

➡️ Distribution costs
➡️ New business growth
➡️ Margins
➡️ Incentives to sell certain products

🔴 Banks & NBFCs

Banks and lenders also came under pressure.

Why?

Because bancassurance and credit-linked insurance generate fee income.

If commissions on these products are sharply reduced and compulsory bundling is restricted that income stream could be affected.

The immediate market reaction has been sharp:

But the bigger story is what the paper says about the future of insurance distribution in India.

IRDAI believes the current distribution architecture is falling short on two key objectives:

1. Improving policyholder welfare

2. Expanding insurance coverage across the country

The regulator has also been increasingly focused on high distribution costs, mis-selling, transparency and customer outcomes.

The proposed reforms go beyond simply changing commission structures. IRDAI is looking at a broader overhaul of distribution, with greater focus on:

→ Distribution efficiency
→ Market conduct & transparency
→ Customer outcomes
→ Stronger competition
→ Digital platforms & interoperable infrastructure
→ Data-driven underwriting

The interesting part: IRDAI wants technology to play a bigger role in reducing transaction costs and making insurance more accessible, transparent and affordable.

This could have implications not just for PB Fintech and Turtlemint, but also for InsuranceDekho, which is preparing for an IPO.

However, this is still a consultation paper, not final regulation. The proposals can change after stakeholder feedback.

The direction, though, is worth watching: insurance distribution is increasingly being treated as a structural efficiency issue rather than just a commission/regulatory issue.

Policybazaar Shares Fall 26% on IRDAI Proposals

Policybazaar parent PB Fintech shares came under heavy selling pressure, falling around 26%, after IRDAI proposed a wide-ranging overhaul of insurance distribution economics.

Proposed Changes to Insurance Commissions:
IRDAI's consultation paper proposes linking distributor commissions to factors including product complexity, distribution channel, policy size and selling effort.
For health insurance, the proposal includes commission limits of 15%–20% for new policies, while renewal and portability commissions could be capped at lower levels. Motor and life insurance commissions would also face proposed product-specific limits.

Why Policybazaar Is in Focus:
Policybazaar operates primarily as an online insurance distribution platform, making the proposed commission framework particularly relevant to its business economics.
According to Jefferies, a 10% reduction in commission rates could potentially translate into a 10%–12% decline in earnings for PB Fintech and Turtlemint. This is a brokerage estimate, not a confirmed impact.

IRDAI Also Targets Distribution Costs:
The regulator has proposed a five-year reduction in Expense of Management limits, alongside greater disclosure of commission structures and stronger safeguards against mis-selling.

The proposals also include restrictions on volume-linked incentives, commission clawbacks in cases of mis-selling, and greater use of digital infrastructure such as Bima Sugam.

The consultation process is currently open, with stakeholders invited to submit comments by October 25, 2026. These are proposals and are not yet final regulations.

Insurance stocks crashed today 📊

HDFC Life -7%
PB Fintech leading losses
SBI Life, LIC, ICICI Pru, Max Financial all under pressure

Most posts will stop at the headline.

Here's the next layer 👇

What actually happened:

IRDAI issued a CONSULTATION PAPER titled:
"Recalibrating Economics of Insurance Distribution"

3 big proposals inside:

1️⃣ Ban on "dark patterns" (misleading online selling tactics)
2️⃣ Lower Expense of Management (EoM) limits
3️⃣ Commission structure reforms + transparency mandates

Why the market panicked:

Bernstein flagged commission cuts as "far more severe than expected."
That directly hits:
✅ Insurer margins (EoM squeeze)
✅ Distributor economics (lower commissions)
✅ Aggregator business models (PB Fintech, Turtlemint)

The two things retail is missing:

⚠️ Point 1: It's a CONSULTATION PAPER
Not law. Not final. Not effective tomorrow.

IRDAI historically softens proposals after industry feedback.

Look at June 2024 reforms HDFC Life ended up welcoming them after softening.

⚠️ Point 2: Impact ≠ Uniform
- Bancassurance-heavy insurers (SBI Life, HDFC Life) less exposed
- Online aggregators (PB Fintech) MOST exposed
- Traditional agent-driven insurers (LIC) least exposed
The market dumped all of them equally today.
That's a mispricing signal — not a fact.

What to actually watch next:

📍 Industry response window (usually 30-60 days)
📍 Final EoM % (the number that decides margins)
📍 Bancassurance carve-outs (banks are lobbying hard)
📍 Q2 pre-sales commentary (will show real impact vs perception)
📍 Bernstein / MS / JPM revised target updates

The lesson every trader should take from today:

Regulatory panic days = maximum information asymmetry.
The people who read the actual circular (not the headlines) get the real picture.
Most retail reads the % move.
Institutions read the fine print.

Read the paper. Not the tweets.

Save this for reference 📌

#ShantiGold #SHANTIGOLD  #jewellery  

Shanti Gold trades at around 12x trailing earnings. Its closest listed peers trade at 27-37x. That gap is worth understanding, because the forward numbers don't obviously justify it.

Building FY27E and FY28E off management's own guided ranges from the Q1 FY27 call (not independent volume assumptions): 

Base case has FY27E revenue at ₹3,129 Cr (+55% YoY), EBITDA ₹238 Cr at a 7.6% margin, PAT ₹163 Cr, EPS ₹21.2.
FY28E steps up further — revenue ₹4,224 Cr (+35%), EBITDA ₹329 Cr at 7.8%, PAT ₹245 Cr, EPS ₹31.9 — as the Marol facility (commissioned Jun-2026, capacity more than doubled to 6,700 kg p.a.) and the Jaipur plant (targeted Nov-Dec 2026) move toward fuller utilisation. That's real, guided earnings compounding, not a hopeful extrapolation.

On the peer gap specifically: at 12x trailing P/E, Shanti Gold trades at roughly a third of Sky Gold & Diamonds' 36.9x and under half of Motisons Jewellers' 27.1x — despite posting the highest ROCE in that set (33.5% vs 27.0% and 14.5%). The structural tailwind behind all three names is the same one: organised gems & jewellery's share of the market is projected to rise from ~35% to ~60% by CY29, on a market growing ~9.7% CAGR — and as a BIS-hallmarked, design-led B2B supplier to large organised retailers, Shanti Gold sits directly in that formalisation trend, with capacity now largely funded and multiple new products/geographies (Turkish jewellery, plain gold, North India, Dubai exports) still barely priced in.

Worth being straight about why the gap hasn't closed already: a 13-month listed track record, structurally negative operating cash flow (management-confirmed, tied to the hold-ready-inventory model), and one guided quarter that hasn't fully played out yet are genuine, priced-in reasons for caution — not just an information gap the market hasn't noticed. 
That's exactly why the next 2-3 quarters of guided-margin delivery matter more here than for a peer with a longer history.

How big is the semiconductor equipment opportunity? 

According to SEMI, an industry body, the semiconductor equipment market is expected to move from ~US$117bn in CY25 to US$166bn in CY26 with sustained growth momentum through CY28 to reach a record of ~US$230bn. 

How is India benefiting from the equipment manufacturing boom?

As widely known, the global semiconductor equipment market is influenced by complex import-export dynamics with US/Netherlands dominating exports for critical tools while APAC region is a major importer for fabrication/testing.

This is followed up with export restrictions from US to China for any of the equipment, makes it extremely viable for them to set up their alternate supply chains in other countries, like India which is backed by government initiatives.

Importantly, while these companies also have their facilities in SE Asian nations, they are yet looking at India as an alternate hub due to the severe talent crunch, and rising costs of production globally vs a conducive environment domestically.

This trend in turn helping specialized EMS players to benefit, as players like LAM, Applied materials and other key players are looking for local partners for exports.

Looking only at the headline interest rate can be misleading. Before accepting a personal loan, compare:

Annual interest rate / APR

Processing fee

GST and other applicable charges

Prepayment / foreclosure charges

Late-payment and penal charges

Loan tenure

Total repayment / EMI

Actual lender behind the app

RBI guidance also requires regulated digital-lending arrangements to disclose the loan's Annual Percentage Rate (APR) and certain other costs and data practices.

This matters because a customer who once bought just a sink can now be sold an entire kitchen ecosystem, and cross selling across these categories tends to lift both revenue per customer and overall margins over time.

Domestic India business is still relatively underpenetrated. Revenue here grew from 65 crores in FY21 to 178 crores in FY26, a compounded growth rate of over 22%, and management is targeting 500 crores by FY29 or FY30. This growth is being driven by an expanding dealer network of over 5,000 dealers, more galleries and franchise service centres, a stronger online presence and a genuine Make in India push for appliances and faucets. Since India is a much smaller part of the business today compared to exports, this segment has a long runway ahead.

Newer categories of kitchen appliances and faucets are growing much faster than the legacy sink business. Appliance volumes grew 48% and steel sink volumes grew 59% over the last four years, compared to 20% for the flagship quartz sink category. As these smaller but faster growing categories become a bigger share of the overall mix, they should pull up the company's blended growth rate and profitability since appliances and faucets typically carry better margins than a mature commoditized product.

Carysil has been steadily winning new global partnerships that were not there before. It has become the sole supply partner for global names like Howdens, Karran and Lowe's in quartz sinks, increased its wallet share with IKEA's global quartz supply, and added fresh relationships with Home Depot in the US and Canada, Amazon USA, and Hafele in both India and Australia and New Zealand. Each of these represents a large, established retail channel that can scale volumes quickly once the relationship deepens, which is a meaningful trigger for both revenue and better capacity utilization.

Real operating leverage still to be unlocked. Capacity utilization currently stands at 88% for quartz sinks and 91.6% for steel sinks, which are already high, and the company is expanding installed capacity further by 2.5 lakh units in quartz and 1.5 lakh units in steel sinks. Since a large part of manufacturing costs are fixed, running expanded capacity at high utilization tends to disproportionately boost profit growth compared to revenue growth, which explains why EBITDA has compounded faster than revenue historically.

The overseas subsidiaries, especially United Granite in the US and the newer Carysil FZ LLC in the UAE, are still early in their scale up journey. UAE revenue has grown from just 2 million AED in FY24 to 10 million AED in FY26, showing this is a genuinely young growth vector rather than a mature one, and any further scale up in these newer international markets can add incremental growth on top of the core India and UK business.

Put together, a widening product basket, an underpenetrated domestic market with an aggressive dealer expansion plan, fast growing new categories, marquee new global retail partnerships, and high but still expanding capacity utilization are the key ingredients management is counting on to sustain double digit revenue and profit growth in the years ahead.

Q1 FY27 Operating PAT ₹609 Cr (+14% YoY), while Asset Management + Private Wealth PAT jumped 44% YoY. Group AUM reached ₹4.5L Cr (+34%), with AMC + Wealth increasingly driving earnings.

2️⃣ AMC compounding is accelerating 📈
AMC AUM is nearing ₹2L Cr, SIP run-rate is ~₹16,000 Cr annually and SIP flows grew 16% YoY. Management expects high AMC growth to continue through FY27 as more funds cross the 3-year track-record threshold.

3️⃣ Multiple catalysts ahead 🚀
₹3,000 Cr private-credit fund is nearing final close, expected in Q2 FY27. Commercial real-estate fund is planned for H2 FY27. Private Wealth AUM is already ₹2.4L Cr (+37%), while distribution assets crossed ₹45,000 Cr.

4️⃣ Visibility improving 💰
Management expects ~₹66 Cr/quarter of variable-return contribution for the next 3 quarters, subject to realization. Meanwhile, Wealth/AMC/Alternates provide increasing recurring earnings. IB deal pipeline remains a wildcard upside catalyst.

🎯 Thesis: #MOFSL is gradually becoming an AMC + Private Wealth + Alternatives compounding platform, reducing dependence on pure broking/trading income.

Two Different Signals

The RBI’s KYC change and SEBI’s compliance easing address a specific kind of friction: how hard it is, operationally, for a foreign investor to open an account, certify documents, and start trading in India. The September outflow is being driven by a different set of forces entirely, global interest rates, crude prices, and currency movements, that have very little to do with how easy India’s paperwork is.

Easier paperwork doesn’t offset a stronger dollar. The two trends aren’t really in tension with each other so much as they’re operating on entirely different timelines, one structural and slow-moving, the other cyclical and driven by global conditions that change month to month.

Riding the Infrastructure Wave: Unlocking Man Industries' Multi-Year Growth Blueprint

The global line pipe sector is undergoing a massive structural shift. Driven by intense energy security mandates in the Middle East and heavy public utility outlays in India, Man Industries (India) Ltd. has repositioned itself from a standard regional exporter into a localized, cross-border manufacturing platform.

This breakdown covers the physical capacities, structural value-mix changes, long-term valuation modeling, and the future growth opportunities for Man Industries up to FY32 and beyond.

Scaling the Factory Floors: Capacity & Revenue Ceilings

Historically, Man Industries operated a baseline capacity of 1.20 Million Metric Tonnes Per Annum (MTPA), heavily centered on standard carbon steel submerged arc welded (SAW) pipes in India. Under this legacy setup, pricing limits and competitive domestic bidding restricted the absolute revenue ceiling to roughly ₹4,500 – ₹4,800 Crores.

Following the acquisition of Saudi Arabia's National Pipe Company (NPC) and key infrastructure expansions, the global operational blueprint scales to 1.63 Million MTPA. More importantly, the company is optimizing this total tonnage across premium nodes:

1. The Jammu Greenfield Plant: A specialized facility adding 22,000 MTPA of high-margin Stainless Steel Seamless Pipes and Tubes, targeted for full commercialization by early FY28.

2. The Dammam Coating Node: A localized value-added coating plant in Saudi Arabia that shifts production from bare pipes to insulated, high-yield anti-corrosion lines.

The Capital Result: By shifting production toward higher-priced stainless steel and integrated pipe coating systems, the company's maximum physical revenue potential expands to a ceiling of ₹11,500 Crores at peak optimal utilization.

Increasing capacity utilizations over next 5 years: 

Management has provided near-term guidance of ₹5,000 – ₹5,500 Crores in revenue for FY27, backed by an explicit projection of 25% to 35% growth in FY28. Over the long term, the company aims to move utilization up to its absolute physical cap.

Assuming a 20% CAGR in revenues over next 5 years backed by a stable 15% margins (due to premium product mix), reducing finance cost, we can expect a EPS CAGR of 25-30%. 

Order Book Backbone Needed to Match This Growth 

To support this upward trajectory, the underlying order engine must expand to ensure execution visibility:

Current Backlog: The company holds a solid ₹3,600 Crore order book, backed by a massive ₹24,000 Crore bidding pipeline (70% focused in the high-yield MENA region).

FY32 Required Backlog: To reliably sustain a manufacturing output of ₹11,500 Crores, the rolling order book needs to scale to a steady baseline of ₹8,500 – ₹9,500 Crores, requiring a global active bidding pool that continuously hovers around ₹45,000 Crores.

Breaking the Ceiling: Post-FY32 Growth Opportunities

Once Man Industries hits 100% capacity utilization at its ₹11,500 Crore ceiling, it cannot grow further through standard domestic volume scaling. Post-FY32, the company's next phase of growth will likely shift to non-volume levers to capitalize on secular tailwinds:

1. Pure Pricing Power & Alloy Premiumization

Even with a fixed volume of 1.63 Million MTPA, the company can mix-shift its output toward high-value Corrosion Resistant Alloy (CRA) lined pipes used for deep-water and highly sour gas fields. This transition shifts the growth driver from volume to value, supporting a steady 3% to 5% price-led organic revenue CAGR.

2. Service-Heavy "Coating-Only" Revenue Mix

Instead of acting purely as a steel processor, the company can utilize the specialized Dammam Coating Facility to coat bare line pipes manufactured by third parties. Because this model excludes the pass-through cost of raw steel plates, it expands corporate margins toward 18–20%, generating substantial cash flow with minimal extra capital requirements.

3. Launching Phase 3 Global Capex Modules

By FY32, the business will be highly deleveraged, generating significant free cash flow. This financial flexibility position allows management to launch a Phase 3 Greenfield module—potentially establishing localized ERW/SAW manufacturing hubs in emerging infrastructure areas like North Africa or the Americas, structurally lifting the revenue ceiling past ₹15,000+ Crores.

4. Capturing the Transnational Hydrogen Pipeline Shift

The global pivot toward green hydrogen requires high-pressure, zero-permeability pipeline networks. Man Industries' early move into certified metallurgy positions them to capture these high-margin, specialized infrastructure allocations as global utilities begin updating their networks over the coming decade.

Summary: Core Investor Takeaways & Valuation Triggers

For Man Industries to maintain its valuation and capture long-term upside, it must achieve three core operational triggers:

1. Structural ROE Improvement: The business must move away from historical 9–10% ROEs to stabilize within the 18–20% bracket. This requires the high-margin Jammu Stainless Steel and Saudi Dammam Coating lines to operate at high utilization while cash flows from Merino Shelters help pay down peak debt.

2. Scaled Order Book Backlog: The current ₹3,600 Crore backlog only secures short-term targets. To sustain its 5-year growth path toward peak capacity, the company must convert its ₹24,000 Crore MENA bid pipeline to maintain a rolling order book of ₹8,500 – ₹9,500 Crores.

3. Phase 3 Capex Announcements: Current projects cap the ultimate revenue potential at a hard ceiling of ₹11,500 Crores. Announcing a Phase 3 Greenfield module using generated free cash flow would lift this ceiling and provide a major valuation rerate by extending the volume growth phase.

Valuations and momentum - my thoughts.

I will take example of Sansera Engineering, a stock which I missed despite tracking closely.

I tracked Sansera for a long time. I knew about the growing order book and increasing traction in Aerospace, Defence & Semiconductors (ADS)
But I didn't buy it as I didn't think there was enough juice left.
At the time, it was trading at **35–40x P/E**, and I thought that was already expensive.
I could not have been more wrong.
Yesterday I checked it again: **~82x P/E.**
I had to rub my eyes a couple of times to believe !!

The mistake wasn't in understanding the business. 
**It was underestimating how far a strong growth story can rerate when the market is gung-ho about tailwind sectors.**

Sansera is still predominantly an auto-ancillary company. ADS is growing rapidly, but it is still a relatively small part of the overall business.
FY26 revenue was roughly **90% Auto and 10% ADS**. ADS is growing rapidly, but even at 18–20% of revenue by FY28, Auto will still be the majority of the business.
And it is not as if Sansera is growing at 50 or 100%. 
It will probably grow at 20-25% CAGR for next few years (that too depends on the auto sector cyclicality)

Yet the market has rewarded the growth visibility with a massive valuation expansion.

And this is something I'm thinking about much more now. Sansera is just one example, but there are many many more where valuations have been rerated to twice their historical averages and the stocks are still going up.

**Valuation-based entry and exit strategies does not work particularly well in sectors with strong structural tailwinds, high growth visibility and strong price momentum.**

I have learnt my lessons. I no longer use valuations as an exit strategy, because to be honest, it does not work well in sectors with strong momentum 

I have several stocks in my current portfolio where I believe valuations are already in the **highly overvalued zone**.
But I'm not exiting just because of that.
I might book partial profits in some cases if I feel like rotating into other opportunities.
But, my exit is mostly based on trailing stops, but I want to **stay with the momentum as long as the underlying growth story and price trend remain intact, because nobody can predict how far the stock in a strong uptrend will run, as evident with Sansera**
The market doesn't care what P/E you think is fair.
Let market decide what valuations it wants to pay, who am I to decide?

**In a strong growth cycle, the biggest risk may not be paying an expensive valuation. It may be exiting a winning stock simply because it looks expensive.**

posts.text:
On this day in 1994 we lost the great Robert Bloch.

His reputation is so tangled up with Psycho (and understandably so) that most people don't have a clue what an exceptional and protean writer he was.

Cosmic horror, ghost stories, psychological horror, all manner of thrillers, folk horror, gothic horror and horror that has yet to be adequately bundled into some neat and tidy subgenre, Bloch was an exceptional talent.

He was a protégé of H. P. Lovecraft, a man who is often denigrated as cold but who was profoundly nurturing. Bloch was only 20 when Lovecraft died; I wish Lovecraft had lived longer, if only to see what he had helped encourage.

Oswal Pumps — a business I am watching, but staying away for now

Oswal Pumps is a vertically integrated solar-pumping and renewable-energy company. Its core business is manufacturing submersible pumps, monoblock pumps, electric motors, solar modules, pump controllers and other BoS components, and then supplying complete turnkey solar pumping systems. It also manufactures many of these components in-house, giving it more control over the product and supply chain.

The company has supplied 1.19 lakh solar pumps under various government schemes and has a distributor network of around 1,406 distributors.

Q1 FY27 was weak:

Revenue: ₹473.6 Cr | -7.9% YoY
Operating EBITDA: ₹74.3 Cr | -47.2% YoY
Operating EBITDA margin: 15.7% vs 27.4%
PAT: ₹53.8 Cr | -43.1% YoY
PAT margin: 11.2% vs 18.4%So 

while the company remains profitable, both revenue and profitability declined sharply. The company supplied around 43,077 pumps in Q1, including 19,724 solar pumps and 23,353 non-solar pumps.

Why are margins under pressure?

There are several headwinds.

1. PM-KUSUM 2.0 delay:
This is a major issue because solar irrigation has been a key growth engine.

2. Aggressive bidding in Maharashtra's Magel Tyala scheme:
Management said competitive bidding resulted in around 9% lower realisations.

3. Higher raw-material costs:
Geopolitical conditions have increased input costs. 

Management estimated the Q1 margin impact at roughly 8–9% from aggressive bidding, 3–3.5% from higher raw-material costs and another 1–1.5% from operating leverage. The company is trying to diversify
This is probably the most important part of the story. Oswal is moving beyond its dependence on government solar irrigation and entering:

PM Surya Ghar → Rooftop Solar → Utility Solar → C&I Solar EPC → Solar Channel Sales → Wires & Cables

It is also evaluating the Jal Jeevan Mission, where management sees an addressable opportunity of around 42,000 pumps. The company has already created a dedicated PM Surya Ghar vertical. Current order book across rooftop, utility and C&I solar is around 72 MW, with a broader pipeline of 359 MW. Management is targeting around 2 lakh households under PM Surya Ghar in FY27, with estimated revenue potential of roughly ₹800–1,000 Cr from this opportunity. It is also using its existing spare capacity to enter wires and cables, without significant additional capex.

Capacity & capex:

The company has 570 MW of existing solar-module capacity. The first phase of the module expansion is 1 GW, targeted for commercial production in September 2026, while the pump & motor capacity expansion and automation programme is expected to be completed by Q3 FY27.

Total FY27 capex is expected to be around ₹360–400 Cr, with the IPO-funded expansion plans progressing.

Guidance:

Management has maintained: FY27 revenue growth: 20–25%
FY27 operating EBITDA margin: 15–17%
FY27 PAT margin: 11–13%

Management expects Q2 revenue to grow more than 10–15% YoY, with stronger growth expected in the second half. Beyond FY27, it is targeting 30–40% medium-term growth. 

Management also says that if PM-KUSUM 2.0 eventually launches, margins could improve from the guided range, although it has not quantified how much. But execution is the question
This is where I remain cautious. I had this company earlier, but I sold it after seeing the repeated deterioration in the business and the gap between management expectations and actual execution. 

The medium-term opportunity looks good on paper: PM-KUSUM 2.0 + PM Surya Ghar + rooftop + C&I + utility solar + new products + capacity expansion

But execution and timing remain crucial.PM-KUSUM 2.0 was expected earlier. In August, management was expecting it during Q2, while as recently as 9 September 2026, the Union Renewable Energy Minister was still saying the new version would be launched “soon.” And that repeated delay matters because the industry had built expectations around the scheme. 

My view:

The medium-term guidance looks attractive, but the near-term picture remains challenging. Revenue is down, margins have compressed sharply, competitive intensity is high, raw-material costs remain elevated and PM-KUSUM 2.0 continues to be delayed. I will continue tracking Oswal Pumps closely, but for now I am staying away. The numbers I want to see improve before changing my view are: Revenue growth → order execution → realisations → EBITDA margin → receivables/cash conversion → PM-KUSUM 2.0 rollout.That will tell us whether the diversification strategy is actually reducing the company's dependence on one government-led scheme.

How do you catch (or at least ride) such rude bull runs?

Technical lessons since listing:

- Long base & consolidation (2021–mid 2025) after IPO volatility — classic accumulation.

- Volume expansion + higher highs/lows on the monthly.

- Complex structure (labelled L/H/S) that ultimately resolved *up* with a clean breakout + follow-through.

- Momentum phase once it cleared the multi-year range — parabolic but still supported by volume.

Fundamental lessons:

- Started as a solid precision auto-component player (2W/PV/CV connecting rods etc.).

- Quietly built a high-margin growth engine in Aerospace + Defence + Semiconductor (ADS).

- ADS order book exploded to ₹4,400–5,750 Cr range while still a small % of sales → operating leverage + margin expansion.

- Clean balance sheet, professional management, consistent execution, and structural tailwinds (exports, localisation, defence, semis).

- Revenue & PAT compounding accelerated once the new verticals scaled.

How to identify the next ones:

1. Quality business + clean books at IPO.

2. Visible new growth vector (new segment/geography/customer) that is still small but has a large order book or runway.

3. Multi-year base on higher timeframes with rising volume on breakout.

4. Management that keeps delivering and reinvesting.

Not advice. Just pattern recognition + homework.

Know Your PMS: Carnelian Shift Strategy

The idea
A mid and small cap focused portfolio of 25 to 30 stocks, spread across sectors and built to ride structural trends. Carnelian blends two kinds of businesses: "Magic" companies in a phase of accelerated growth and "Compounder" companies growing steadily, bought at what it calls a reasonable price (its QGARP style, short for Quality Growth at a Reasonable Price). From 23 March 2026 the investment objective was broadened to cover structural shifts across the Indian economy and the changing global macro environment, giving the strategy more room beyond its original manufacturing and technology themes.

The manager
Manoj Bahety is a co-founder of Carnelian, a chartered accountant and a CFA charterholder with more than 26 years in financial services, including about 11 years at Edelweiss Securities, where he headed forensic, thematic and mid cap research. Risk is managed through CLEAR, Carnelian's proprietary forensic framework.

The portfolio
Where the money sits: pharma & CDMO (contract drug manufacturing) 27.2%, engineering & capital goods 20.4%, IT 15.2%, auto & auto ancillary 12.1%, consumption 6.8%. Average market cap ₹65,221 Cr, median ₹18,604 Cr. Carnelian expects the portfolio companies' earnings to compound 27.3% a year over FY26 to FY28, against 15.9% for the BSE 500 (AMC estimates), with net debt to equity of 0.0 and a PEG of 1.1 on FY28 estimates (P/E divided by earnings growth). "Order book of ₹X crore" is one of the most-quoted numbers in every results headline, and one of the least understood. It's a funnel, not a single number — and where a rupee sits in that funnel matters as much as the total.

Take Raymond Realty: the company discloses a total project pipeline (GDV) of ~₹52,000 Cr. But of that, only ~₹28,000 Cr is actually launched, only ~₹12,300 Cr of that is sold, and only ~₹9,000 Cr has been recognised as revenue in the P&L so far. Four different numbers, four different stages of certainty — and the headline GDV figure is the least useful one for near-term earnings, because unlaunched land and signed-but-unlaunched JDAs (₹24,000 Cr of the total) haven't even started generating cash flow yet.

Astra Microwave's ₹4,341 Cr order book looks like one clean figure, but CRISIL's own rating rationale breaks it into an execution schedule: ₹150 Cr from the Uttam radar programme is expected in FY27, rising to ₹450 Cr by FY30 — a single order spread across five years, not a lump sum landing next quarter. Meanwhile "confirmed" and "expected" are doing very different work in the same sentence: Virupaksha Radar and an anti-drone system are "expected in the next few months," which is a forecast, not a booked order.

Ramkrishna Forgings is a good example of the opposite problem — a number that's genuinely unconfirmed being cited alongside confirmed ones. The company has an 80,000-wheel confirmed Railways order for its Rail Wheel JV. Press reports separately cite a 20-year, 1.54-million-wheel contract for the same JV — a number the company itself hasn't confirmed on any call. Treating both as equally real overstates the visibility by more than an order of magnitude.

The questions worth asking before an order-book headline moves your view of a stock: is this confirmed-in-hand, or a bid/pipeline/press figure? What's the execution timeline — is ₹1,000 Cr landing next quarter or over five years? And is revenue recognition tied to delivery milestones (common in engineering/EPC/real estate) or booked upfront? A ₹5,000 Cr order book executing over six months is a completely different business than the same number executing over six years — even though it's the same headline.
