Paul then tells us what heavenly citizens are expecting: “from whence also we look for the Saviour, the Lord Jesus Christ.” That sentence ought to settle the argument for anyone willing to let the words stand. We look toward Heaven because the Saviour comes from Heaven. We do not look toward the Mediterranean for the rise of the Beast. We do not look toward Jerusalem for permission to expect Christ. We do not look toward Brussels, Rome, Moscow, Babylon, Washington, or a computer laboratory. We look for the Saviour. The word “also” joins the heavenly citizenship with the heavenly expectation. Our Head is there, our home is there, and the One for whom we wait is there. The passage is not about the soul going to Heaven at death. It is about Christ coming from Heaven to transform the body. Death separates the soul from the body; the coming of Christ reunites and glorifies the whole redeemed person.

Christ “shall change our vile body, that it may be fashioned like unto his glorious body.” That is the completion of bodily redemption. The soul of the believer is saved, the spirit is made alive, and the body has been purchased, but the body remains mortal, corruptible, weak, and subject to death. Romans 8 says we groan within ourselves, “waiting for the adoption, to wit, the redemption of our body.” First Corinthians 15 says the corruptible must put on incorruption and the mortal must put on immortality. That change takes place “in a moment, in the twinkling of an eye.” No seven-year endurance course is inserted into Philippians 3. No Antichrist appears between our heavenly citizenship and our transformed body. The text moves directly from looking for the Saviour to the Saviour changing our vile body. A system that forces the Beast into that sentence is not interpreting Scripture. It is smuggling unwanted baggage through customs.

4. When He Appears, We Shall Be Like Him

First John 3 begins with present certainty and future expectation: “Beloved, now are we the sons of God.” Sonship is not a prize waiting at the end of a probationary Christian life. The believer is a son now. He has been born of God, accepted in the Beloved, sealed by the Spirit, and made an heir of God and a joint-heir with Christ. Yet John immediately admits that the full glory of this position has not appeared: “it doth not yet appear what we shall be.” The Christian carries eternal life inside a dying body. He possesses a heavenly standing while walking through a fallen world. He is already seated in heavenly places in Christ, yet his feet still get tired, his body still grows old, and his flesh still wars against the Spirit. Salvation is complete as a purchased possession, but all its effects have not yet been manifested.

2. The Blessed Hope Is a Person

Biblical hope is not wishful thinking. When a man says, “I hope it does not rain,” he is admitting uncertainty. When the Bible speaks of the believer’s hope, it speaks of a settled expectation founded upon the promise and character of God. Titus 1:2 calls it the “hope of eternal life, which God, that cannot lie, promised before the world began.” The Christian does not hope for eternal life because he is unsure whether God will provide it. He hopes because God promised it, God cannot lie, Christ purchased it, and the Holy Spirit sealed the believer unto the day of redemption. Biblical hope is faith looking forward. Faith takes God at His word concerning what He has done; hope takes God at His word concerning what He will do. Both rest upon the same infallible authority. If God could lie about Christ’s coming, He could lie about Christ’s cross. If His future promises are uncertain, His past accomplishments are no safer. The entire Christian life stands or falls upon the trustworthiness of the words God gave.

The blessed hope is inseparable from Jesus Christ Himself. Paul calls Him “Lord Jesus Christ, which is our hope” in 1 Timothy 1:1. Colossians 1:27 says, “Christ in you, the hope of glory.” The Christian is not merely waiting for an event; he is waiting for a Person. The Rapture is blessed because Christ comes. The transformation of the body is blessed because Christ performs it. Heaven is blessed because Christ is there. Eternal life is blessed because it is life with Christ. Strip Christ from the doctrine and you have nothing left but a timetable. Prophecy without Christ becomes religious arithmetic—men counting horns, heads, weeks, months, kingdoms, and earthquakes while missing the Lord of prophecy. The testimony of Jesus is the spirit of prophecy. The Bible’s prophetic program does not exist to entertain curious minds but to reveal the glory, authority, victory, and return of God’s Son.

This is why the title “The Blessed Hope Is Not the Antichrist” strikes the real nerve. Some teachers will protest that they do not call Antichrist their hope. Of course they do not use those words. They simply construct a system in which the Church cannot expect Christ until the Antichrist has first appeared, made his covenant, entered his temple, displayed his abomination, persecuted the saints, enforced his Mark, and ruled his kingdom. They deny the title while teaching the substance. Their believer goes to bed listening for the hoofbeats of the Beast while Paul’s believer listens for the shout of the Lord. Their believer studies how to recognize the Mark; Paul’s believer studies how to be found blameless at Christ’s coming. Their believer waits for the man of sin; Paul’s believer waits for the Son of God. Call it whatever respectable theological name you please; if Jesus Christ cannot come until Antichrist comes first, then the Antichrist has become the Church’s practical expectation. The Bible will have none of it.

Park Medi World - Key Insights

Park Medi World, through its wholly owned subsidiary, has signed a 28-year O&M agreement to operate Axis Hospital & Research Centre in Kanpur. The hospital has 300 beds and ~1.2 lakh sq ft of built-up area.

Park is not acquiring the land/building. It will invest in renovation, modernisation and medical equipment, then operate the facility. 

This allows Park to add beds with substantially lower upfront capital than a greenfield or owned-hospital model.

The agreement provides for:
🔹6% of collections as revenue share to AES
🔹Minimum guarantee of ₹20 lakh/month inclusive of GST in Year 1
🔹Thereafter ₹20 lakh/month + GST.

The company is using this deal to build density in Uttar Pradesh, where it already sees a healthcare infrastructure gap. Kanpur provides a large urban/semi-urban catchment and expands Park's UP presence.

Park currently operates 17 hospitals/~4,300 beds. Along with the Kanpur facility, the company says it is integrating 6 additional hospitals and expanding 3 existing units, which together are expected to add 2,300 beds, taking potential network capacity to 6,600 beds.

The expansion strategy is shifting toward a mix of owned + PPP + asset-light O&M models, rather than relying exclusively on capital-heavy greenfield hospitals.

What I'd track next
=> Renovation/equipment capex for Kanpur
=> Commissioning date — targeted by end-FY27
=> Occupancy ramp-up of the 300 beds
=> ARPOB and specialty mix
=> EBITDA margin at the Kanpur facility
=> Total capex per added bed across the 2,300-bed expansion pipeline
=> How much of the 2,300 beds is owned vs PPP vs asset-light
=> Whether the asset-light strategy translates into higher ROCE/ROIC

The potential operating leverage could be meaningful if the new hospitals ramp occupancy and margins without requiring proportionate balance-sheet investment.

India’s New-Age Economy Could Triple to Nearly $300 Billion by FY31

India’s next big economic story may not come only from banks, IT, manufacturing or infrastructure.

A new layer of the economy is being built across digital commerce, fintech, consumer brands, quick commerce, AI, electric mobility and tech-led platforms.

India’s new-age companies generated roughly:
$33 Bn revenue in FY22
$100 Bn in FY26
$300 Bn by FY31E

That implies roughly 25% annual growth over the next five years.

And the ecosystem supporting this growth is already in place.

India’s online retail market has reached roughly $80 Bn, supported by more than 300 Mn annual online shoppers, while UPI now processes more than 20 Bn transactions every month.

This digital infrastructure is allowing companies to scale much faster.

Consumer brands founded in 2016 took around 6.8 years to reach ₹100 Cr revenue.

For brands founded in 2020, it took only around 3.4 years.

The number of new-age consumer brands above ₹100 Cr revenue could increase from roughly 90 in FY22 to 500 by FY31.

But scale alone is not enough.

India’s new-age economy has largely proved that it can grow revenues.

The next challenge is profitability.

Aggregate EBITDA improved from roughly -$4.8 Bn in FY23 to +$1.4 Bn in FY25, but profits are still concentrated in a few sectors such as BFSI.

Even at $300 Bn revenue by FY31, the overall profit pool is estimated at only around $5–10 Bn.

So the real test will be whether these businesses can convert growth into sustainable margins and cash flows.

And this transition is already visible in Indian stock markets.

Some new-age companies listed last year, while several more have entered the public markets this year:

🔹Swiggy & Eternal Ltd: Food Delivery & Quick Commerce
🔹Groww: Digital Investing
🔹Lenskart:  Omnichannel Consumer Brand
🔹Urban Company:  Services Marketplace
🔹PhysicsWallah: EdTech
🔹Ather Energy: Electric Mobility
🔹Shadowfax: E-Logistics Platform
🔹Fractal Analytics: AI & Analytics
🔹MobiKwik: Fintech
🔹ESDS Software Solution: Cloud & Data Centre Infrastructure

A decade ago, many of these business models barely existed at scale.

Today, they are becoming part of India’s listed-market universe.

And the pipeline remains large.

New-age companies already account for roughly 25% of Indian IPO proceeds, and this share could move towards 40% by CY30.

Combined public and private fundraising could approach $50 Bn annually by the end of the decade.

At the same time, more scaled private businesses are becoming potential IPO and M&A candidates.

The bigger story is clear:
👉Startups are becoming companies.
👉Digital brands are becoming national brands.
👉Private businesses are entering public markets.
👉And technology is becoming embedded across every layer of India’s economy.

India’s new-age economy reaching nearly $300 Bn by FY31 is a powerful headline.

But the real winners will be the businesses that turn that growth into durable profits, cash flows and competitive advantages.

This Indian Factory Ships 300 Million Parts a Year — To 45 Countries📈

A company you’ve probably never heard of makes parts that could be inside your car, a fighter jet, a surgeon’s tray, and a missile — sometimes all in the same week. 

Meet INDO-MIM🔥

The scale first, because the numbers alone are wild: 650+ customers. 45+ countries. Over 10,000 different parts made. More than 300 million units shipped every single year. This isn’t a factory — it’s a manufacturing ecosystem.

👉So what do they actually make? 

Think tiny, precise metal and ceramic components — not the big stuff, the small stuff that has to be perfect. Gears, brackets, surgical instrument parts, defence components — pieces so exact they’re measured in microns.

Their core superpower is called Metal Injection Molding (MIM). 
Take metal powder, mix it with a binder, injection-mould it into shape (like how plastic toys are made), then heat it until the binder burns off and the metal fuses solid. Result: complex metal parts, made by the millions, cheap and precise.

For parts too big or specialized for MIM, they switch to Investment Casting & Precision Machining — pouring molten metal into a mould built around a model, letting it harden, then machining it to exact tolerances. Old-school metalworking, upgraded.

👉Product Portfolio -

•MIM (Metal Injection Molding): 

Making metal parts the way toy factories make plastic figures — mix metal powder with a binder, inject it into a mold, then bake the binder away so only solid metal remains. Lets them mass-produce tiny, complex metal parts cheaply.

•Investment Casting & Precision Machining: 

The classic way to make metal parts — pour liquid metal into a mold, let it harden, then fine-tune it with cutting tools. Used for bigger or more specialized parts that MIM can’t handle.

•CIM (Ceramic Injection Molding): 

Same trick as MIM, but with ceramic instead of metal — for parts that need to survive extreme heat or wear without melting or breaking down.

•3D Printing: 

Building a part layer by layer straight from a digital design — great for prototypes or one-off shapes that would be hard to make any other way.

•Tooling: 

Making the molds and dies that every other process above actually needs — the “tools that make the parts.”

•Metal Powders: 

They manufacture their own raw metal powder, the core ingredient for MIM- giving them control over quality and cost from the very first step.

👉Where do all these parts go? 

Automotive — 24.61% of FY26 revenue. Defence — 18.69%. 
Medical — 18.08%. 
Aerospace — 11.96%. 
Consumer Products — 10.80%. 

Four completely different industries, one supply chain.

👉Now the money.💰 

Q1 FY27 (just one quarter) tells an even better story. Revenue: ₹12,187.42 million, up 9.39% from ₹11,140.98 million a year earlier. Solid, not spectacular.

But profit? 
Profit after tax jumped to ₹2,401.22 million — up 31.64% from ₹1,824.10 million. Profit grew 32%. That gap is the single most bullish line in this entire report.
It’s called operating leverage. 🔥

Translation: once a factory like this crosses a certain volume, each extra part costs less to make, because the fixed costs — machines, buildings, R&D — are already paid for. 

👉Where’s the next leg of growth coming from? 

Three bets:

① Medical — acquired Phoenix DeVentures II Inc. to move into medical device prototyping, a higher-margin business.

② Defence & Aerospace — a new arm, INDO-MIM Arms Components Pvt Ltd, built specifically for this sector.

③ A digital quoting portal — customers upload drawings, get instant quotes. Management calls it a “game changer” for winning new business.

👉Bottom line: 

A company quietly making 300 million tiny, precise parts a year, feeding cars, jets, missiles, and medical devices — growing profit 3x faster than revenue, with low debt and real expansion plans.

Jižní velitelství izraelské armády opevňuje pozice podél žluté linie a pokračuje v cílených úderech. Hamás mezitím obnovuje svou správu v oblastech mimo izraelskou kontrolu. Téměř tři roky po 7. říjnu zůstává ozbrojený a ovládá kolem 30 % Pásma Gazy.

Pokud odzbrojení v rámci dohody podporované Spojenými státy selže, armáda může dostat rozkaz vynutit je silou. Náčelník generálního štábu Ejal Zamir proto požaduje připravenost rychle přejít z obrany do rozsáhlejší ofenzivy. Od zahájení pozemní operace v Gaze padlo 472 izraelských vojáků.

Podél žluté linie, která podle příměří vymezuje rozmístění izraelských sil, vznikají dlouhodobá opevněná stanoviště. Armáda zároveň útočí na příslušníky Hamásu a jeho infrastrukturu. Velitelé se snaží udržet ostražitost vojáků vyčerpaných opakovaným nasazením a zabránit tomu, aby přechod od manévrových bojů k předsunuté obraně vedl k polevení.

Hamás upevňuje svou moc také příjmy z obchodu. Do Gazy denně vjíždí přibližně 600 vozů s humanitární pomocí. Podle izraelských bezpečnostních odhadů vybírá Hamás na kontrolních stanovištích ze zboží poplatky, které někdy dosahují téměř 50 procent.

Jednání tak zůstávají zablokovaná. Benjamin Netanjahu a ministr obrany Jisrael Kac odmítají obnovu Gazy před odzbrojením Hamásu a demilitarizací pásma.

Customers aren’t really buying metal

Precision

Qualification

₹55 Cr of annual revenue potential from components already developed or under development

More customers

Titagarh Rail Systems × BHEL — New Long-Term Vande Bharat Update 🚆

Titagarh Rail Systems and Bharat Heavy Electricals have signed a JV agreement for the long-term maintenance of 80 Vande Bharat Sleeper trainsets.

Key points:
• ₹24,000 Cr contract awarded by Indian Railways to the TRSL-BHEL consortium
• Scope: Manufacturing + supply of 80 Vande Bharat Sleeper trainsets
• Maintenance period: 35 years
• New JV company formed for maintenance
• Titagarh Rail Systems: 50%
• BHEL: 50%
• Maintenance includes operation of manufacturing units & trainset depots + comprehensive maintenance

The bigger point 👇
This is not just a train manufacturing order. The contract also creates a 35-year lifecycle maintenance opportunity, giving Titagarh Rail Systems and BHEL a long-term role in the Vande Bharat Sleeper ecosystem.

Vande Bharat Sleeper is aimed at modernising long-distance rail travel with better passenger comfort, technology and operational efficiency.

🪟 एक बेईमानी के बाद दूसरी बेईमानी आसान क्यों हो जाती है?

कल्पना कीजिए...

एक इमारत की एक खिड़की टूट गई।
किसी ने उसे ठीक नहीं किया।

🧱 कुछ दिनों बाद दूसरी खिड़की भी टूट गई। दीवार पर कोई लिख गया। सड़क पर कचरा पड़ा रहने लगा।

अब वहाँ रहने वाले लोगों को एक संदेश मिल रहा है:

_“यहाँ किसी को परवाह नहीं है।”_

*यही विचार ब्रोकन विंडोज़ इफ़ेक्ट के नाम से प्रसिद्ध हुआ।*

👥 1982 में जेम्स विल्सन और जॉर्ज केलिंग ने तर्क दिया कि किसी जगह पर दिखने वाली छोटी-छोटी अव्यवस्थाएँ लोगों को यह संकेत दे सकती हैं कि यहाँ नियमों की निगरानी कमजोर है।

और जब लोगों को लगता है कि कोई नहीं देख रहा, तो छोटे नियम तोड़ना आसान हो सकता है।

लेकिन यहाँ एक महत्वपूर्ण बात है।

*इसका अर्थ यह नहीं कि:*
“एक टूटी खिड़की अपराध पैदा करती है।”

🔎 बाद के शोधों में इस सिद्धांत के कई हिस्सों पर बहस हुई है। अपराध और अव्यवस्था के पीछे गरीबी, संस्थागत कमजोरी, बेरोज़गारी और सामाजिक परिस्थितियों जैसे कई कारण हो सकते हैं।

फिर भी इसका एक सवाल हमारे रोज़मर्रा के जीवन में बहुत गहरा है।

🗑️ अगर सड़क पर पहले से कचरा पड़ा है, तो क्या हमें भी कचरा फेंकना थोड़ा आसान लगता है?

🚶 अगर पूरी लाइन में लोग नियम तोड़ रहे हैं, तो क्या हमें भी नियम तोड़ना उतना गलत लगता है?

🏢 अगर किसी जगह में छोटी बेईमानी को लगातार नजरअंदाज किया जाता है, तो क्या बड़ी बेईमानी के लिए भी भीतर प्रतिरोध कम हो सकता है?

लेकिन ब्रोकन विंडोज़ इफ़ेक्ट का गहरा सवाल केवल सड़क की टूटी खिड़की से नहीं, हमारे भीतर से शुरू होता है।

बाहर की टूटी खिड़की कहती है:
“यहाँ किसी को परवाह नहीं है।”

🪞 *लेकिन भीतर की टूटी खिड़की?*

एक बार झूठ बोला।
एक बार बेईमानी की।
फिर उसे सही ठहरा दिया “सब करते हैं।”

🔄 *अगली बार वही करना थोड़ा आसान हो गया।*

क्यों?

क्योंकि अब अहंकार को सिर्फ गलत काम नहीं बचाना है, अपने पुराने चुनाव से बनी हुई अपनी पहचान भी बचानी है।

🔄 एक गलत चुनाव के बाद उसी दिशा में दूसरा गलत चुनाव करना आसान, और उससे पलटना मुश्किल होता जाता है।

एक चुनाव के बाद अगला चुनाव अक्सर उसी “मैं” को बचाने के लिए होता है।

📌 „Druhý nejvyšší schodek“ je zavádějící argument
Opakovaně zaznívá, že plánovaný schodek státního rozpočtu je druhý nejvyšší v historii. Takové srovnání považuji za ekonomicky velmi problematické.

Srovnává totiž nominální částky v různých letech, přestože se mezitím výrazně změnila cenová hladina i velikost české ekonomiky. Pro posouzení fiskální pozice je relevantní především deficit celého sektoru vládních institucí v poměru k HDP – nikoliv absolutní částka schodku státního rozpočtu.

Deficit vládního sektoru kolem 3,5 % HDP by byl nepochybně vysoký a dlouhodobě jej nelze udržovat. Není ale pravda, že by taková hodnota stavěla Českou republiku do nějaké bezprecedentní fiskální situace.

Současně je nutné dodat, že rozpočet ještě není definitivně schválen. Za jeho konečnou podobu nese odpovědnost celá vláda.

📊 97 % příjmů rozpočtu pohltí mandatorní a kvazimandatorní výdaje
To je podle mě mnohem důležitější číslo než samotná nominální výše schodku. Pokud mandatorní a kvazimandatorní výdaje odpovídají přibližně 97 % příjmů státního rozpočtu, prostor pro každoroční hledání úspor bez legislativních změn je mimořádně omezený.

Z toho plyne poměrně nepříjemný závěr: z hlubokých strukturálních deficitů se dlouhodobě nedostaneme bez změn zákonů a parametrů některých veřejných politik.

Stále zastávám názor, že konsolidace by měla probíhat především na výdajové straně. Vzhledem k velikosti problému se zřejmě nevyhneme ani některým opatřením na straně příjmů. Jejich rozsah by ale podle mého názoru měl být menší než rozsah úprav veřejných výdajů.

📉 Dluhová dynamika České republiky je zatím stále relativně příznivá
Objevují se tvrzení, že česká dluhová dynamika je již sama o sobě nepříznivá. S tím nesouhlasím.
Pro vývoj poměru dluhu k HDP je zásadní mimo jiné vztah mezi úrokovou sazbou z dluhu a nominálním růstem ekonomiky.

Pokud se efektivní nominální úroková sazba českého státního dluhu pohybuje kolem 3,5 %, zatímco nominální HDP roste přibližně o 5–6 %, samotný efekt úroků a ekonomického růstu působí na poměr dluhu k HDP stále příznivě.

Jinými slovy: při nulovém primárním saldu by tento mechanismus sám o sobě poměr dluhu k HDP snižoval.
Problémem jsou ale značné přetrvávající deficity, které tento příznivý efekt převáží. Proto je potřeba je postupně snižovat.

Za rozumný kompromis považuji, že vláda v prvních rozpočtech promítá priority, pro které získala politický mandát, ale současně se ve fiskálně-strukturálním plánu zavázala k následnému snižování deficitů.

📌 Fiskální pravidla nejsou samospasitelná
Dlouhodobě upozorňuji, že česká národní fiskální pravidla byla do značné míry „gumová“. Nejde o ústavní zákon a parlament může zákonná pravidla změnit.

Zajímavé je, že velmi podobnou argumentaci nedávno použil také ekonom David Marek, bývalý poradce prezidenta republiky. V rozhovoru pro Český rozhlas ze 4. září upozorňoval na omezený význam samotných národních fiskálních institucí a pravidel pro skutečnou udržitelnost veřejných financí.

Jeho argumenty: a) nikdy jsme žádná rozpočtová pravidla neměli, jelikož to nebyl ústavní zákon a není problém ten stávající zákon změnit, b) ani zákon o rozpočtové odpovědnosti ani Národní rozpočtová rada nejsou relevantní instituce pro zachování udržitelných veřejných financí.

📌 Pohonné hmoty: problém je dnes jinde než před několika měsíci
Situace na trhu pohonných hmot se mezitím změnila.
Hlavním problémem dnes nejsou neobvykle vysoké marže čerpacích stanic, ale především crack spread – tedy rozdíl mezi cenou ropy a cenou výsledných rafinérských produktů. Jinými slovy, významná část tlaku vzniká už na úrovni rafinérií.

Možnosti České republiky ovlivnit tento faktor jsou omezené. Pokud by měl stát reagovat daňově, větší ekonomický smysl by proto dávalo koordinované evropské řešení než izolované české zásahy.

Higher US yields can make dollar assets more attractive, putting pressure on FPI flows, the rupee, Indian bond yields and equity valuations. FPIs have already net sold nearly ₹14,475 crore of Indian equities in September after buying in July and August.

A weaker rupee, meanwhile, can amplify imported inflation particularly with crude already elevated.

UPI’s zero-MDR era has effectively ended for a segment of merchant payments.

The UPI Steering Committee has fixed MDR at 40 bps for merchant transactions above ₹2,000, capped at ₹300 per transaction. The fee is payable by merchants, while payments up to ₹2,000 remain free.

At 40 bps, the ecosystem could generate up to ₹16,000 crore annually. Moneycontrol’s analysis shows transactions above ₹2,000 account for only 2.5% of UPI transactions but nearly ₹6 lakh crore about 67% of merchant UPI value.

That makes the policy significant not because it affects most UPI payments, but because it targets the relatively small slice carrying a disproportionate share of transaction value.

Let’s talk about the Vizhinjam Port in India—a masterclass in modern engineering that shows us how the future is built completely from scratch.

Here are the hard facts that blow your mind and expand our vision of global scale:

⚖️ Scale: Vizhinjam vs. PanamaWhile Panama’s port system handles a massive ~9.9 million TEUs annually (historically connecting two oceans), Vizhinjam is charging full speed ahead toward its goal of 5.7 million TEUs projected by 2028 in its final phase. Its purpose isn't to cross continents like Panama, but to prevent India from relying on third parties, becoming South Asia’s deep-water transshipment super-hub built to welcome 24,000+ container marine monsters.
👥 Employment & SalariesThe human engine behind the beast: it generates over 2,000 current direct and indirect jobs, aiming to add 5,500+ positions by 2028. What does specialized operational talent make? An automated crane operator or high-level port technician in India earns salaries ranging from $500 to $1,200 USD per month (well above the local average, attracting elite talent).

🧠 Why is it different? (Born on the Tech Crest)Old ports carry legacy obsolescence. Vizhinjam was born right in the middle of a tech boom: it's a native digital port.
Who runs it? Owned by the Government of Kerala (VISL), but its commercial and logistics operations are concessioned for 40 years to the Indian giant Adani Ports (APSEZ).

Who does R&D & Tech? Global partners like ABB (crane automation) and Kaleris (AI-powered optimization software) lead innovation agreements.
Key Tech: Remote control crane cabins with computer vision (no operators hanging 40 meters in the air), smart OCR gates, and real-time predictive bottleneck analysis.

🌱 The Green Energy RevolutionVizhinjam isn't just digital; it's eco-friendly. It is integrating infrastructure for green bunkering (production and storage of green hydrogen, green methanol, and green ammonia), 100% electric machinery powered by captive solar and wind sources, and zero-emission internal fleets.

📢 Risk Associated with buying the unlisted company shares for Pre-IPO....

1️⃣ Delay in IPO
2️⃣ Valuation stays same for longer period
3️⃣ Promoter dilutes more & more
4️⃣ Company doesnt meet its projected numbers
5️⃣ You can't trade or exit as no buyers
6️⃣ No price transparency
7️⃣ You pay higher tax if u sell unlisted shares
8️⃣ You pay higher price / commission to brokers

✅ So please don't rush behind Pre-IPOs, consider Pre-IPOs as long term investment.

Titagarh Rail Systems Limited (TRSL) has officially executed a Joint Venture Agreement (JVA) with Bharat Heavy Electricals Limited (BHEL) on 15th September 2026. This strategic partnership aims to establish a Joint Venture Company (JV Company) where both TRSL & BHEL will hold an equal 50% shareholding. 📊

𝗞𝗲𝘆 𝗔𝘀𝗽𝗲𝗰𝘁𝘀 𝗼𝗳 𝘁𝗵𝗲 𝗝𝗩:

- 𝗣𝘂𝗿𝗽𝗼𝘀𝗲: The JV Company will focus on the comprehensive maintenance of 80 Vande Bharat Trainsets, a critical part of the "Manufacturing cum Maintenance of 80 Vande Bharat Trainsets including Upgradation of Government Manufacturing Units & Trainset Depots and Comprehensive Maintenance for 35 years" project awarded by Indian Railways. 🚆
- 𝗗𝘂𝗿𝗮𝘁𝗶𝗼𝗻: The agreement includes a significant 35-year comprehensive maintenance program, providing long-term revenue visibility.
- 𝗖𝗮𝗽𝗮𝗯𝗶𝗹𝗶𝘁𝗶𝗲𝘀: This collaboration will combine the complementary strengths & railway sector expertise of both TRSL & BHEL. 🚂
- 𝗦𝘁𝗿𝗮𝘁𝗲𝗴𝗶𝗰 𝗔𝗱𝘃𝗮𝗻𝘁𝗮𝗴𝗲 𝗳𝗼𝗿 𝗧𝗥𝗦𝗟: The JV offers TRSL an opportunity to solidify its position in the maintenance & lifecycle support segment of the railway industry, expanding its participation across the rolling stock value chain from manufacturing to long-term service. 🚀
- 𝗢𝗽𝗲𝗿𝗮𝘁𝗶𝗼𝗻𝗮𝗹 𝗦𝘆𝗻𝗲𝗿𝗴𝗶𝗲𝘀: The partnership is expected to foster technical collaboration, operational synergies, & efficient lifecycle management of the Vande Bharat Trainsets, aligning with Indian Railways' vision for modern passenger transportation. 💡
- 𝗝𝗩 𝗦𝘁𝗿𝘂𝗰𝘁𝘂𝗿𝗲: The JV Company will be incorporated as a Private Limited company with an initial paid-up share capital of ₹50,00,000. TRSL & BHEL will each nominate two directors to the JV's Board. 🏢

This joint venture marks a significant step for Titagarh Rail Systems Ltd. in strengthening its foothold in the crucial maintenance segment of the Indian railway sector.

I got a few messages regarding my opinion on Gaja Alternative Asset Management Ltd. 

I don't have any stake in the business. I applied for the IPO, but didn't get even a single lot  and honestly, I'm quite happy that I didn't. 😉

The results were also bad so a thumbs down on that too.

Ok, let's come to understand its business model : 

In simple words : 

Iska business model ICICI Prudential AMC jaisa hi hai. Capital investors se raise karo, us capital ko manage/deploy karo aur AUM par fees earn karo. 

AUM grows faster than costs, operating leverage kicks in and profits can scale disproportionately.

But yahan ek BIG difference hai. Traditional AMC mein earnings largely management fees par depend karti hain, whereas GAJA ke paas carried interest ka bhi engine hai. Matlab portfolio companies achha perform karein, exits strong aayein, toh GAJA ko investment profits ka ek share milta hai. 

Isliye earnings thodi lumpy ho sakti hain, but successful exits ke time upside bhi kaafi powerful ho sakta hai.

So don't value GAJA simply as another AMC. 

Think of it as an asset manager with private equity carry machine. Recurring management fees provide the base, while carry can create the real earnings upside.

No recommendation. Please DYODD.

Heartfelt Tribute to *Bharat Ratna Sir M. Visvesvaraya (1861-1962)* - India's first great engineer-statesman:

*1. As an Engineer:*
- *Krishna Raja Sagara (KRS) Dam, Mysore (1924):* Designed and built one of the largest reservoirs in India at that time across the Kaveri river. It had automatic sluice gates he patented.
- *Flood Protection System for Hyderabad (1909):* After the devastating Musi river floods, his flood-control system saved the city. It is still the basis of Hyderabad's water system.
- *Block System of Irrigation:* Invented the automated floodgates and block irrigation system, first installed at Khadakwasla Dam, Pune.
- *Mysore to modern industry:* He was the architect of many industries in Mysore.

*2. As Diwan of Mysore (1912-1918) - Made Mysore a Model State:*
- *Mysore Iron and Steel Works (now VISL) at Bhadravati* - India's first major steel plant.
- *Mysore University (1916)* - One of India's first universities.
- *Government Engineering College, Bangalore (1917)* - Now UVCE, one of India's first engineering colleges.
- *Established* Mysore Chamber of Commerce, Mysore Soap Factory, Mysore Sandal Oil Factory, Bangalore Agricultural University, State Bank of Mysore.

*3. Nation Building Vision:*
- Wrote the books "Reconstructing India"and "Planned Economy for India" in 1920 and 1934 - he was the first to propose economic planning for India, 15 years before formal planning started.
- Advocated for compulsory education, industrialization, and technical education.

*Honours:*
- Bharat Ratna in 1955, Knight Commander (KCIE) by British, and his birthday *15th September is celebrated as Engineer's Day* in India.

He is remembered for his principle: "Work is worship."

'Targeting 15% ROE as We Scale Up Loan Book'

Q&A with Pankaj Gadgil, MD & CEO, Aditya Birla Housing Finance — on growth targets, portfolio mix, AI and efficiency

Growth Outlook — Next Two Years
Target: AUM of ₹1 lakh crore over next 8–10 quarters — implies CAGR of 25–40% depending on timeline (two to two-and-a-half years)

Targeting 15% ROE with ROA reaching ~2.4%

Focus on maintaining asset quality and improving profitability while scaling

Key Levers for Growth
Currently 209 points of sale — adding minimum 100 branches this year (67 already launched)

Added ~1,000 employees — employee base now ~5,900

₹2,750-crore capital infusion from Advent International sufficient for next 18–24 months as AUM moves towards ₹1 lakh crore

If CAGR maintained at 35–40%, additional capital will be required after two years

Incremental borrowing of ₹20,000–22,000 crore needed as AUM moves from ₹48,000 crore to ₹68,000–70,000 crore

Borrowing & Liability Profile
Will continue to diversify liabilities

NCDs account for ~45% of liability profile

Term loans 32%, NHB funding 12%, short-term funding 11%

Portfolio Mix — Prime, Affordable & Construction Finance
Decided to remain a full-stack player

Current mix: Prime 47%, Affordable 38%, Construction Finance 15%

No significant change expected — Prime could move to ~45%, construction finance to remain at 15–16%

Within affordable housing, lowest-ticket informal-income segment currently ~6% of portfolio — expected to rise to ~11% over next 8–10 quarters

AI — 22 Use Cases in Housing Finance
Currently 22 AI use cases in housing finance — 13 live spanning:

Acquisition, underwriting, portfolio management

Customer service, sales coaching

Software development, audit and compliance

Objective: improve productivity even as capacity is added

Efficiency Gains from Technology
Cost-to-loan-book ratio declined from 2.93% at end of FY25 to ~2.21%

Ambition: bring this down to 1.7% over next 8–10 quarters

Technology, digital and AI critical to achieving that

AI Impact Across Aditya Birla Capital
Health insurance: AI processes nearly 74% of cashless claims; 35%+ of pre-authorisation requests processed straight-through

Life insurance: 100% of new-business processing is digital; ZARA bot collected ~₹411 crore in renewal premium during Q1 FY27

Agentic voice bots: enabled 90%+ first-call resolution; generated ₹1,500+ crore in impact across renewal premium, GMV and AUM

Mutual funds: Disha platform contributed to 12% incremental portfolio creation

Next Big Focus Area in AI
Building an enterprise-wide knowledge layer so data created for one use case can be used across others

Also focusing on ontology and semantic layers, data engineering and APIs

El Logos (desde Heráclito hasta los estoicos y la teología clásica) es el principio de inteligibilidad, orden y simetría que gobierna la totalidad del cosmos. Si quisieras buscar un análogo budista al Logos, tendrías que hablar del Dharma (la ley cósmica y la verdad de la realidad) o de la Tathatā (la talidad del ser), jamás de la conciencia fenoménica condicionada (Vijñāna).

El Ser sustancial de Shankara no es lo mismo que la Vacuidad sin alma de Buda:
- El Vedanta afirma el Ser Absoluto (Brahman) y la identidad del Yo supremo (Ātman). Y para tu sorpresa el propio Vedanta invoca que el Ser (Sat) es inseparable de la Conciencia y la Inteligibilidad (Chit, el Logos).
- El Budismo, en cambio, defiende el No-Ser / No-Alma (Anattā) y la Vacuidad (Śūnyatā). Niega radicalmente que exista un Ser o un Absoluto sustancial.

Decir que el Ágape es el ser y no el Logos es una contradicción. El Ágape no es una sustancia ciega. Ágape es un concepto griego-cristiano que define el Amor de auto-donación y generosidad. Ni el budismo ni el vedanta usan la palabra Ágape (usan Karuṇā o Maitrī).
Si separas el Ágape del Logos, ¿qué le queda? Un amor sin inteligibilidad, sin dirección, sin verdad y sin discernimiento. Eso no es amor, es pulsión ciega, caos emocional o voluntarismo arbitrario. El Ser no es solo Logos (lo que sería un racionalismo estéril) ni solo Ágape (lo que sería un fideísmo ciego). El Logos y el Ágape son co-eternos y consustanciales. La Verdad engendra Amor, y el Amor se manifiesta en la Verdad.

Apelas a Hipatia de Alejandría como si fuera una maestra de la no-dualidad budista o del Ágape sin Logos. Hipatia fue una matemática, astrónoma y filósofa de la escuela Neoplatónica de Alejandría (seguidora de Plotino y Porfirio). Plotino enseñaba que del Uno (To Hen) emana en primer lugar el Nous: la Mente Divina, el Intelecto Supremo que contiene todas las Formas e Ideas inteligibles... ¡es decir, el LOGOS! Para los neoplatónicos como Hipatia, el orden matemático del cosmos y la contemplación intelectual del Nous eran el camino sagrado hacia el Uno. Afirmar que Hipatia enseñaba que "el logos no es el ser, es ilusión" es escupir sobre toda la obra matemática y neoplatónica por la que ella vivió y murió. Hipatia era una sacerdotisa del Logos matemático, no una nihilista lingüística.

✨🪔 WHEN MOTHER GAÑGĀ’S LIGHT REACHED THE THAMES 🪔✨

13 September 2026 will be remembered as a historic day for Hindus in the United Kingdom.

For the first time, the sacred tradition of Gañgā Ārtī was brought to the River Thames in London, transforming the historic Royal Steps at the Old Royal Naval College, Greenwich, into a breathtaking scene of dīpa, mantra, bhajan and devotion.

And what made the evening even more extraordinary was the unity it represented.

Spiritual leaders, saints, Hindu organisations and communities from across the UK came together in one sacred space.

The occasion received support and blessings from organisations representing the extraordinary diversity of the Hindu tradition — including Anoopam Mission, Arsha Vidya UK, BAPS Swaminarayan Sanstha, Brahma Kumaris, Hindu Swayamsevak Sangh (HSS), ISKCON, International Vedanta Society UK, Parmarth Niketan and Sanskruti Foundation.

At the heart of the ceremony was Pujya Swami Swaroopananda, Global Head of Chinmaya Mission, who led the Aarti, alongside Brahmacharini Shripriya Chaitanya, Resident Teacher of Chinmaya Mission UK, and the many spiritual and community representatives (Swami Chidanand Saraswatiji, Parmarth Niketan Ashram in Rishikesh) who gathered in the spirit of Sanatan Dharma — unity in diversity.

Two rivers. Two civilisations. One offering.
The Gañgā is not merely a river in Hindu consciousness. Gañgā represents life, purity, knowledge, compassion and the eternal flow of Dharma.

Bringing Gañgā Ārtī to the Thames was therefore not about replacing one river with another. It was about carrying the devotion, gratitude and spiritual consciousness associated with Mother Gañgā across geographical boundaries — into the heart of London.

And then came a moment that many presents will not forget.

🌧️ As the Ārtī unfolded, rain descended over the Thames.
The lamps continued to glow. The chants continued to rise. The devotees remained immersed in prayer. For many watching, it felt almost as though Mā Gañgā herself had come to shower her blessings upon the gathering. 

Perhaps the most powerful message of the evening was not simply that a centuries-old tradition had reached London.

It was that Hindus of different sampradayas, organisations and traditions could stand together before one common altar of devotion.

As Swami Swaroopananda reminded the gathering, when we come together in devotion, differences fall away and the deeper spirit of oneness, love and harmony shines through.

🌍 And the world was watching. The event was streamed internationally, reaching audiences far beyond the banks of the Thames, while thousands gathered in person for what was described as London's first-ever Gañgā Ārtī.

This was more than a ceremony.
It was Sanatan Dharma in its most beautiful expression — tradition without division, devotion without boundaries, and unity without uniformity.

🪔 From the banks of the Gañgā to the banks of the Thames.
✨ A light was offered.
🙏 A tradition was carried forward.
🤝 Hindu unity was witnessed.
🌧️ And perhaps, just perhaps, Ma Gañgā answered with her blessings.

Har Har Gañge
Jai Mā Gañge

Morena y sus propagandistas intentan minimizar el desplome educativo. Ninguna de sus excusas resiste los datos.
Dicen que una prueba estandarizada no permite comparar países. Es absurdo: para eso se estandariza. PISA no mide todo. Mide tres cimientos: comprensión lectora, razonamiento matemático y conocimiento científico a los 15 años. Sin ellos, lo demás difícilmente se construye. Además, permite comparar a México consigo mismo desde 2000.
Culpan a las pantallas. Pero pantallas hay en todas partes y no todos cayeron. Asia mantiene resultados extraordinarios. Brasil, antes debajo de México, ya nos superó en lectura; Colombia, en ciencias.
También dicen que la caída fue pequeña. La comparan con 2022, cuando México ya se había derrumbado. Frente a 2018, perdió 21 puntos en matemáticas, 12 en lectura y cinco en ciencias.
Su última coartada es la inclusión: sostienen que el promedio bajó porque entraron más jóvenes marginados. Es falso. La proporción de estudiantes de 15 años dentro de la escuela aumentó de 63% a 76% entre 2015 y 2018. Con Morena cayó a 75%. El desastre llegó con menos alumnos, no con más.
El daño es todavía mayor. La reforma educativa de 2012-2019 había detenido una caída de más de 10 años y comenzado a elevar los aprendizajes, sobre todo en matemáticas en las escuelas públicas. Bedoya, De Hoyos y Estrada demuestran que el Servicio Profesional Docente mejoró la selección de maestros y el aprendizaje matemático.
Morena no solo provocó un desplome: destruyó un instrumento que funcionaba.
La primera destrucción está fuera de PISA. En 1921, México inició un siglo continuo de expansión educativa. Todos los gobiernos, de Obregón a Peña Nieto, aumentaron la cobertura. Morena rompió esa marcha: preescolar cayó de 72% a 61%; primaria, de 96% a 93%; secundaria se estancó y bachillerato retrocedió dos puntos.
Duplicaron el presupuesto de becas, pero redujeron casi a la mitad el apoyo recibido por los estudiantes más pobres. Márquez-Padilla, Parker y Vogl muestran que sustituir Prospera disminuyó la asistencia escolar y aumentó el trabajo juvenil informal.
La segunda destrucción fue financiar esa expansión desmantelando otros programas. El caso más cruel son las 25 mil escuelas de tiempo completo. Atendían a cuatro millones de niños: aprendían más, comían mejor y permitían que sus madres trabajaran. Morena las borró. También redujo 92% la formación docente, más de 60% el presupuesto de las normales y recortó el programa de inglés.
La tercera fue pauperizar los planes y los libros: redujeron brutalmente la enseñanza de las matemáticas e impusieron un método de alfabetización anticuado y desarticulado. Debilitaron justo las capacidades que PISA evalúa.
La cuarta fue devolver plazas y promociones al control político y sindical. Separar el poder político de la carrera docente había permitido contratar mejores maestros y elevar los aprendizajes.[1] Morena restauró la arbitrariedad: volvió a someter a los maestros y sacrificó a los alumnos.
La hipocresía completa el retrato. Los hijos de sus políticos estudian en escuelas privadas: jornadas completas, buenos materiales, inglés y maestros libres del yugo sindical. Conservan para los suyos aquello que arrebataron a los pobres.
Ante el desastre, no rectifican. Minimizan, polarizan y mienten. Con Morena, la tragedia continuará.
La reconstrucción de México debe comenzar en la escuela. Una nueva república liberal exige una educación para la libertad: que cada persona tenga los instrumentos para construir, sin subordinación, su propio proyecto de vida.

PAT: ₹27.2 Cr, +35%

Gaja earns from:

Now SEBI has approved its ₹2,500 Cr Fund.

And the recent IPO raised ₹550 Cr, including ₹450 Cr of fresh capital.

This creates an interesting flywheel:

Raise larger funds
→ AUM grows
→ recurring fees grow
→ successful exits create performance income
→ stronger track record helps raise the NEXT fund.

Beautiful when it works. 🔥

Performance income can be lumpy.
By nature AMCs and other market linked businesses do well during market up-cycle only !!

For me the key metric isn't just PAT growth.

It's how the FEE-EARNING CAPITAL compounds over multiple fund vintages.

Renomovaný sovětský a ruský režisér a spisovatel Eduard Topol napsal otevřený dopis americkému prezidentovi Donaldu Trumpovi ohledně Putina a jeho války.

Zde je plné znění dopisu. Bohužel Trump si ho s největší pravděpodobností nepřečte — podle všeho je zvyklý sledovat kreslené filmy a nedokáže vstřebat text delší než dvě věty:

„Vážený pane prezidente! Milý Donalde!

Jako autor padesáti knih a tuctu filmů o Rusku se domnívám, že mám právo se s vámi o toto podělit před vaším setkáním s Putinem.

Měl byste vědět, že nemůže ukončit válku proti Ukrajině — i kdybyste mu předal své sídlo Mar-a-Lago v Palm Beach, Trump Tower v New Yorku a tucet golfových klubů.

A není to proto, že by si nechtěl dát od války pauzu, ale proto, že nemůže.

Protože ruské dějiny zná nikoli z učebnice Medinského, ale tak, jak skutečně probíhaly:

Návrat ruských vojáků z Evropy do Ruska po vítězství nad Napoleonem vedl v roce 1825 k děkabristickému povstání proti carovi.

Porážka Ruska v rusko-japonské válce vedla k revoluci v roce 1905.

Útěk milionu ruských vojáků z rusko-německé fronty během první světové války vedl k abdikaci cara Mikuláše II. a k únorové revoluci v roce 1917.

Mírová smlouva, kterou Lenin podepsal s Německem, umožnila bolševikům popravit celou carskou rodinu.

Návrat sovětských vojáků z Afghánistánu v únoru 1989 znamenal začátek rozpadu SSSR.

Vzhledem k těmto skutečnostem Putin nemůže ukončit válku proti Ukrajině ani poslat své vojáky domů.

Pouze možnost ponechat téměř celou svou armádu v Evropě jako okupační sílu po květnu 1945 zachránila Stalina před poválečným převratem.

Právě proto Putin sní o okupaci Ukrajiny, stejně jako pobaltských států, Finska, Polska a tak dále: aby udržel svou armádu daleko od Moskvy.

Pamatuje si, jak se 525 000 vojáků vracejících se v roce 1989 z Afghánistánu změnilo v „afghánské bandity“, kteří terorizovali celé obyvatelstvo SSSR.

A ví, co se stane, až se z ukrajinské fronty vrátí jeden a půl milionu vojáků — muži, kteří se profesionálně naučili zabíjet, rabovat a znásilňovat.

Válka proti Ukrajině umožnila Putinovi zbavit se dvou milionů svých nejaktivnějších odpůrců tím, že je donutil uprchnout z Ruska; pokud jde o zbývající mladé Rusy, buď je poslal na frontu, nebo je naverboval z vězeňských kolonií.

Dnes je jakákoli válka — ať už proti Ukrajině, pobaltským státům, NATO nebo komukoli jinému — nejlepším prostředkem, jak přimět Rusko podřídit se Putinovi a jeho juntě.

Bohužel vám to před schůzkou s Putinem žádný z vašich poradců nevysvětlí, ale moje argumenty si můžete nechat ověřit u Jacka Matlocka a Michaela McFaula.

Nechci, aby Putin — ten bandita, zloděj a vrah milionů lidí — pokračoval ve své drzé manipulaci, lžích a uvádění mého prezidenta v omyl.

Samozřejmě nejsem vojenský expert ani politolog, ale jsem spisovatel s dobrou pamětí.

Pamatuji si, jak Ronald Reagan, Margaret Thatcherová a papež Jan Pavel II. stlačili cenu ropy na 9 dolarů za barel a dodali Afgháncům rakety Stinger, čímž zastavili tažení Moskvy na Afghánistán a přispěli k rozpadu SSSR.

Pokud chcete zastavit Putina a imperiální ambice — které sdílí nejméně polovina ruského obyvatelstva — musíte udělat totéž: stlačit cenu ropy nejméně na 25 dolarů za barel a dodat Ukrajině zbraně, které jí pomohou porazit agresora.

Pokud jde o vaši touhu po americko-ruském obchodním partnerství: v praxi — nikoli pouze ve slovech — k němu možná nedojde dalších sto let, nebo možná nikdy.

Pokud chcete vědět proč, zavolejte mi; rád vám to vysvětlím.

S úctou

The one who expands into everything.

When your life feels smaller than you imagined, remember this:

Growth does not always look like
getting more.

large enough inside
to hold more of reality.

vistāraḥ means expansion, extension, or vast unfolding — Vishnu as the one through whom the universe spreads into countless forms.

We usually imagine expansion externally.

A bigger career.

More money.

More influence.

More experiences.

A larger life.

But there is another kind of expansion.

The ability to hear something uncomfortable without immediately defending yourself.

To hold two truths at once.

To understand someone without needing to agree with them.

To experience disappointment without allowing it to define your entire future.

To love without controlling.

To change your mind when reality asks you to.

A narrow mind needs life to fit its expectations.

An expanded mind can meet life as it actually arrives.

Perhaps spiritual growth is partly this:

Not forcing existence to become smaller—

but becoming spacious enough
to contain more of it.

To remember vistāraḥ is to ask:

Where has my identity become too small
for what life is trying to teach me?

One name. One truth. One step inward.

vistāraḥ — the one who expands into everything.

The soul does not sign a contract to enter birth and rebirth. 
In Vedanta, samsara is considered beginningless. Avidya makes us identify with the body and mind. From that come desires, desires create actions, actions create karma, and unfinished karma leads to further birth. The cycle can continue for countless lives without automatically making us wiser.

The special value of human birth is that we can finally become aware of this cycle and ask deeper questions: Who am I? Why am I doing all this? What actually lasts? 
That awareness can lead toward dharma, God, self-knowledge and ultimately moksha. Samsara may be beginningless, but it does not have to be endless.

115 Trendlyne Insights. One week. A lot of noise—but also some developments worth investigating.

Every week, markets produce hundreds of corporate events.

The challenge isn't finding information.

It's identifying which events could actually change the earnings trajectory, growth visibility or risk profile of a company.

I reviewed the 115 Insight-category events in Trendlyne's weekly data and filtered them through a fundamental-investor lens.

Here are the developments that caught my attention 

1. ORDER BOOKS: The strongest cluster of developments

Anupam Rasayan

A six-year supply contract with a US specialty-metals manufacturer stands out.

The duration matters.

A multi-year contract potentially provides better revenue visibility, customer stickiness and capacity-utilisation visibility than a one-off order.

The questions to investigate:

→ How material is the contract?
→ What margins does it carry?
→ How much incremental capex is required?

Man Industries
₹600 crore of new orders takes the order book to approximately ₹4,100 crore.
The new orders are roughly 14.6% of the reported order book.

That's meaningful.

But the real question isn't the headline order value.

It's:

How quickly can the order book become revenue—and at what margin?

Power Mech Projects

A ₹970 crore Vedanta Power O&M order for a 1,200 MW thermal plant in Chhattisgarh.

The O&M nature of the contract makes this worth investigating beyond the headline value.

Contract duration, margins, working capital and recurring revenue characteristics will determine the quality of the opportunity.

Dilip Buildcon

A ₹1,800 crore petroleum pipeline order from Odisha to Chhattisgarh.

Large order.

But EPC investors know the equation:

Order value → execution → revenue → EBITDA → working capital → PAT.

The first number alone doesn't tell the investment story.

L&T

An offshore order worth ₹2,500–5,000 crore from ONGC for platforms and subsea infrastructure.

For a company of L&T's scale, one order won't transform consolidated earnings.

But it adds another data point to the broader infrastructure and energy investment cycle.

2. POWER & TRANSMISSION

GE Vernova T&D

A Power Grid order involving a 6,000 MW HVDC terminal station is particularly interesting.

The significance goes beyond one contract.

It provides another indication of large-scale investment in transmission infrastructure.

The chain investors should watch:

Power investment → transmission spending → equipment demand → order inflow → revenue → margins.

3. RENEWABLE ENERGY: Actual orders matter

Shakti Pumps

₹236 crore MSEDCL order for 10,000 off-grid solar water pumps.

This is a very tangible event.

Investors can track:

10,000 pumps
↓
production
↓
deliveries
↓
revenue recognition
↓
margins
↓
cash flow

That's far more useful than simply saying "solar is a growth industry."

Suzlon

A 200 MW wind order from Ayana Renewable Power adds another company-specific data point to the renewable-energy opportunity.

The important question remains whether order growth translates into attractive economics.

Vikram Solar

A 124 MW solar-module supply order for a project in Anantapur provides another piece of evidence of renewable-energy activity.

Again, execution and margins matter more than the headline MW number.

4. JASH ENGINEERING: An interesting smaller-company development

Jash Engineering reported ₹66 crore of orders in August.
Its order book stands at approximately ₹937 crore, with 68% of projects overseas.
That combination deserves attention.
Why?
→ sizeable order-book visibility
→ substantial international exposure
→ less dependence on a single domestic infrastructure cycle
The next question is whether the order book converts into revenue at attractive margins and returns on capital.

5. CAPACITY EXPANSION: Where future earnings may be created

IOL Chemicals
₹350 crore capex to increase ibuprofen capacity by 50%, taking annual capacity to 18,000 tonnes.
This is particularly interesting because investors can model the opportunity:

Capacity +50% → utilisation → realisations → margins → incremental PAT

But the return on the ₹350 crore investment will ultimately determine whether the expansion creates value.

Morepen Laboratories

First expansion phase completed early, increasing API/CDMO capacity by 15%.

Early completion is encouraging.

But the next question is demand.

Capacity without utilisation doesn't create shareholder value.

Gopal Snacks

Adds 19,642 MTPA besan capacity in Nagpur.

What's interesting is the stated benefit of reducing transportation costs and improving efficiency.

So this isn't simply:

capacity → volume.

It could potentially be:

capacity → lower logistics cost → better efficiency → margin improvement.

Premier Energies

A JV to establish a 12 GWh battery-storage facility in Telangana.
This potentially broadens the company's opportunity beyond solar manufacturing.
But large projects also require large capital.

The question is ultimately:

What ROCE will the new capacity generate?

KABRA Extrusion Technik

₹750 crore capex planned in the UAE and Vietnam to expand battery production.

Ambitious.

Potentially meaningful.

But also an event where execution and capital allocation deserve close scrutiny.

6. KALYAN JEWELLERS: Growth through distribution

Kalyan plans to add 84 stores in FY27, predominantly outside South India.

The headline number is impressive.

But investors should ask a better question:

What sales productivity and ROCE will these stores generate?

Store additions create value only when the economics of each new store are attractive.

7. REGULATORY DEVELOPMENTS

Indoco Remedies

Its Goa facility received UK MHRA clearance with zero observations.

For a pharmaceutical company, regulatory outcomes can have an outsized impact.

A clean inspection removes an important source of uncertainty.

Worth investigating whether this can support future utilisation, approvals and revenue.

Lupin

Received US FDA approval for a drug with reported annual US sales of approximately $70.7 million.

Here again, the important question is not simply "approved."

It's:

How much of that market can Lupin capture—and at what margin?

Data Patterns

The Defence Acquisition Council reportedly approved acquisition proposals worth ₹1.1 lakh crore.

Potentially a major industry opportunity.

But remember the chain:

Approval
→ procurement
→ contracts
→ execution
→ revenue

The ₹1.1 lakh crore isn't company revenue today.

8. EARNINGS ACCELERATION

Netweb Technologies

The Forecaster expects Q3 EPS to rise 179% YoY, driven by sovereign AI infrastructure demand.

That's a dramatic expectation.

But expectations need validation.

Watch the sequence:

AI demand → orders → revenue → margins → EPS

If those indicators start appearing in actual results, the thesis becomes much more interesting.

Shyam Metalics

Stainless-steel sales rose 16.4% YoY to 10,920 MT in August.

Pellet sales increased 28%.

Unlike a forecast, these are actual operating datapoints reported in the dataset.

Worth tracking whether the volume momentum persists.

Shiprocket

Q1FY27 net loss narrowed 24% YoY to ₹13.7 crore.

Directionally positive.

But the company remains loss-making.

The real milestone is:

loss reduction → operating profitability → sustainable cash flow.

9. INSTITUTIONAL ACTIVITY

CAMS

Societe Generale ODI and Goldman Sachs reportedly bought 73 lakh shares worth ₹498 crore through a bulk deal.

That's substantial enough to warrant investigation.

But institutional buying should never be treated as proof that a stock is undervalued.

The more useful question:

Does the institutional interest coincide with improving fundamentals?

Swiggy

BNP Paribas and Goldman Sachs reportedly bought ₹1,041 crore worth of shares through bulk deals.

Again—interesting.

But the transaction itself isn't the investment thesis.

Fundamentals and valuation still determine the opportunity.

ASM Technologies

A ₹526 crore preferential issue has been approved for SBI Mutual Fund and three investors.
Institutional participation is interesting.
But preferential issuance also means potential dilution.
Fresh capital + deployment + dilution = the equation investors need to evaluate.

10. COMMODITY DEVELOPMENTS

PCBL

Carbon black prices are reportedly up 26.5% YoY.

Potentially meaningful if higher realisations flow through to margins.

The equation:

Selling price → gross margin → EBITDA → EPS

But input costs need to be considered.

Graphite

GrafTech reportedly raised prices by 30%.

Potentially positive for graphite producers if higher prices are sustained.

But commodity cycles can reverse quickly.

This is a cyclical development—not automatically a structural one.

Hindustan Copper

Higher copper prices amid shortage concerns and a weaker US dollar provide a favourable commodity backdrop.

But commodity exposure brings cyclicality.

11. NOT EVERYTHING IN THE INSIGHTS FEED IS POSITIVE

This is perhaps the most important part.

Coforge

The chairman resigned after the audit reportedly flagged gaps in disclosures to the board.

This is fundamentally different from an earnings miss.

Governance concerns can change the risk profile of an investment.

A falling share price does not automatically make the stock attractive.

Cochin Shipyard

EBITDA margin reportedly falls 848 bps in FY27 because of a greater contribution from lower-margin shipbuilding.

Important lesson:

Order book growth ≠ earnings growth.

Order mix matters.

Margins matter.

Granules

Promoter plans to sell 7%, worth approximately ₹1,500 crore.

Promoter selling isn't automatically negative.

But the size makes the rationale important.

Sri Lotus Developers

Promoter reportedly sold 97 lakh shares worth ₹195 crore.

Again, the key is understanding the reason behind the sale and its implications for promoter ownership.

Cohance Lifesciences

Shamshabad formulations plant received a US FDA Form 483 with four observations.

This deserves monitoring because regulatory observations can potentially affect manufacturing and approvals.

PVR INOX

The stock plunged following reports alleging ₹200 crore of kickbacks involving former executive Pramod Arora.

These remain allegations, and investors should distinguish reported allegations from established facts.

Nevertheless, the development introduces a governance/reputational risk that warrants investigation.

So, what did this week's 115 events actually tell us?

I see five broad themes.

1️⃣ Order visibility remains the strongest theme

Power.

Infrastructure.

Railways.

Defence.

Renewables.

Industrial equipment.

A large number of events involve actual orders rather than vague commentary.

But investors need to go one step further:

Order size × margin × execution period × working capital × repeatability

2️⃣ Capacity expansion is accelerating across several businesses

IOL Chemicals.

Morepen.

Gopal Snacks.

Milky Mist.

Premier Energies.

KABRA.

The opportunity isn't simply identifying companies adding capacity.

It's identifying companies where:

incremental capital → high utilisation → high incremental ROCE → sustained EPS growth.

3️⃣ Renewable-energy demand is increasingly visible through actual projects

Shakti Pumps.

Suzlon.

Vikram Solar.

Enviro Infra.

Premier Energies.

ACME Solar.

The next phase of analysis should be about who captures the economics, not simply who participates in the theme.

4️⃣ Governance deserves disproportionate attention

Coforge is the clearest reminder.

Retail investors can spend hours modelling EPS but overlook governance.

Yet one governance issue can change the entire valuation framework.

5️⃣ The event is only the beginning of the investment process

This is the most important takeaway.

A positive event doesn't mean a stock is attractive.

The process should be:

EVENT
↓
Is it material?
↓
What changes in revenue?
↓
What changes in margins?
↓
What happens to EPS and cash flow?
↓
How much capital is required?
↓
What ROCE can be generated?
↓
What valuation is the market already assigning?
↓

Then decide whether it deserves further attention.

That's how I would use a weekly events feed.

Not as a list of stocks to buy.

As a research funnel.

Note: This analysis is based solely on the weekly Trendlyne events data provided. The developments highlighted are intended as potential areas for further investigation, not investment recommendations. Investors should conduct their own due diligence, including reviewing financials, valuations, cash flows, management quality, regulatory filings and risks before making investment decisions.

"Vážený pane prezidente!

Vážený Donalde!

Jako autor padesáti knih a tuctu filmů o Rusku se považuji za oprávněného informovat vás před vaším setkáním s Putinem.

Měl byste vědět, že Putin nemůže ukončit válku s Ukrajinou, ani kdybyste mu daroval svou vilu Mar-a-Lago na Palm Beach, Trump Tower v New Yorku a tucet vašich golfových holí.

A ne proto, že by nechtěl udělat přestávku ve válce, ale proto, že nemůže.

Protože ruskou historii zná ne z učebnice Medinského, ale tu skutečnou:

Návrat ruských vojsk z Evropy do Ruska po vítězství nad Napoleonem vedl k proticarskému povstání děkabristů v roce 1825.

Porážka Ruska v rusko-japonské válce vedla k revoluci v roce 1905.

Útěk miliónu ruských vojáků z rusko-německé fronty během první světové války vedl k abdikaci cara Mikuláše II. a k únorové revoluci v roce 1917.

Mírová smlouva, kterou Lenin podepsal s Německem, umožnila bolševikům zastřelit celou carskou rodinu.

S návratem sovětských vojsk z Afghánistánu v únoru 1989 začal rozpad SSSR.

Když toto ví, Putin nemůže ukončit válku s Ukrajinou a vrátit domů svá vojska.
Pouze možnost nechat téměř celou svou armádu jako okupační vojsko v Evropě v květnu 1945 pomohlo Stalinovi vyhnout se poválečnému převratu.

Právě proto sní Putin o obsazení Ukrajiny, stejně jako Pobaltí, Finska, Polska atd., aby udržel svou armádu daleko od Moskvy.

Pamatuje si, jak se 525 tisíc vojáků, kteří se vrátili v roce 1989 z Afghánistánu, změnilo v bandity-afgánce, kteří terorizovali všechno obyvatelstvo SSSR.

A ví, co se stane, pokud se půl milionu vojáků, kteří jsou schopni profesionálního zabíjení, loupeží a znásilňování, vrátí z ukrajinské fronty.
 
Válka s Ukrajinou umožnila Putinovi zbavit se dvou milionů svých nejaktivnějších oponentů, které donutil utéct z Ruska a zbytek mladých ruských mužů buď nahnal na frontu nebo naverboval do represivních služeb.

Dnes je jakákoliv válka - s Ukrajinou, s Pobaltím, s NATO - a s kýmkoliv jiným - nejlepším způsobem, jak přinutit Rusko podřídit se Putinovi a jeho juntě.

Bohužel, žádný z vašich poradců vám to před setkáním s Putinem nevysvětlí, ale moje argumenty si můžete ověřit u Jacka Matlocka a Michaela McFaula.

Nechci, aby Putin, gangsterský zloděj a vrah miliónů lidí, nadále drze obelhával vás, klamal a podváděl mého prezidenta. 

Samozřejmě, nejsem vojenský expert ani politolog, ale jsem spisovatel s dobrou pamětí.
Pamatuji si, jak Ronald Reagan, Margaret Thatcherová a papež Jan Pavel II. dokázali snížit cenu ropy na 9 dolarů za barel, dát Afgháncům „Stingery“ a tím zastavit moskevské ovládnutí Afganistánu a zničit SSSR.

Pokud chcete zastavit Putina a imperialistické ambice nejméně poloviny ruské populace, musíte udělat to samé – snížit cenu ropy na nejméně 25 dolarů za barel a dát Ukrajině zbraně, které jí pomůžou rozdrtit agresora.

Co se týká vašeho přání vytvořit americko-ruské obchodní partnerství, nejen slovy, ale v praxi, to se může stát za sto let a nebo vůbec nikdy.

Pokud vás zajímá proč, zavolejte mi, vysvětlím vám to.

S úctou,

EDWARD TOPOLE, občan USA a Izraele.

Seznam Zprávy byly kdysi kvalitní médium, dokud jej vedl Jiří Kubík a reportáže se mohly politikům příčit, ale kvalitu jim upřít nešlo. Dnes jde o manipulativní bulvár, faktické dno a bez větší nadsázky lze některé počiny Seznam Zpráv označit přímo za účelové dezinformace.

Uvedu dva nezpochybnitelné příklady.

Jindřich Šídlo dnes zesměšňuje sněmovní vyšetřovací komisi ke kauze Dozimetr. Rajchl je prý neschopný a Dozimetr šetří kvůli odměně za členství v komisi. Doprovodná grafika nemůže vynechat porno, jizvy a další s Dozimetrem nesouvisející ponížení nenáviděného poslance.

https://t.co/1s04YGYzwO

S Rajchlem je však v komisi dalších 12 poslanců. Mimo jiné Renáta Vesecká, Pavel Žáček nebo Tomáš Helebrant. Jde o zkušené zákonodárce či osobnosti znalé práce státního zastupitelství.

Je téma k smíchu? Rozhodně není - stačí se podívat na některé zdokumentované výpovědí.

“Já ti říkám, Jirko, žádný strachy, když přijdem do Prahy, můžem krást.”

Tato slova pronáší Michal Redl k Jiřímu Fremrovi, pravé ruce Jiřího Pospíšila. Ten obžalován nebyl, ačkoli s Redlem trávil dovolené, Fremr jakbysmet.

"Souhlasím s jejich politikou a znám dobře pana Polčáka. A občas s nimi něco konzultuji. Shání (Polčák, pozn. redakce) nějaké schopné lidi do různých společností… Poněvadž se pohybuji tady ve Zlíně delší dobu, tak v tom jim napomáhám.“

Financování politických stran TOP 09 a STAN z organizovaného zločinu? Obvinění i svědci systém několikrát popsali, věc se nevyšetřuje.

Je tedy komise opravdu k smíchu? Je postup Vrchního státního zastupitelství v Praze v pořádku? Je to ostatně jen a pouze státní zastupitelství, které může rozhodnout o poskytnutí či neposkytnutí podkladů. Žalobci se rozhodli neposkytnout jediný papír.

Pokud by se zjistilo, že v kauze Dozimetr účelově přehlíželi trestnou činnost popsanou ve výpovědích svědků, padaly by hlavy na nejvyšších místech.

Ha, ha, ha, směje se Jindřich Šídlo a připravuje další podcast s Janem Dobrovským, největším sponzorem hnutí STAN. Pojďme se všichni pořádně zasmát, jak je Rajchl neschopný.

Padni, komu padni? Nezávislá a objektivní žurnalistika? Jakékoli další obranné manévry proti útokům Andreje Babiše na Seznam Zprávy nebudou fungovat. Viníkem je vedení Seznam Zpráv, nikdo jiný.

Kdyby výše uvedené nestačilo, mám tu druhý příklad.

Nedávno na Novinkách vyšel článek o plánovaném převratu v Černé hoře, který měli plánovat Rusové. Součástí celého komplotu bylo usmrcení proevropského a proaliančního politika Mila Djukanoviče.

"V podivném převratu hráli roli Rusové, uniformy se našly v Srbsku"

Z textu by se skoro zdálo, jako by Rusové převrat a usmrcení Djukanoviče také plánovali.

Střih, klapka, přesouváme se do let 2018 a 2019. Denník N vydává rozsáhlou reportáž o tom, že převrat ve skutečnosti plánoval marketér Zuzany Čaputové (!!!). Světe, div se, totožný marketér měl zajišťovat i kampaň Petra Pavla.

Aron Shaviv byl obžalován a USA jej do Černé hory odmítly vydat. Jen díky tomu je zřejmě dnes i na svobodě. Na Shavivově výplatní pásce byli Michal Repa a Martin Burgr.

https://t.co/o7fRxUdljc

Aron Shaviv svůj podíl na Pavlově kampani zmiňuje na vlastních webových stránkách vedle "úspěchů" ve volbách v Kambodži, Kongu, Bangladéši nebo v zemích afrického Sahelu - samé výkvěty demokracie.

Ale ne, Shaviv neexistuje, Repa s Burgrem dnes provozují "hodnotový" marketing a za vše mohou Rusové a Srbové. Jen škoda, jsou tehdejší články Denníku N a dalších balkánských zdrojů archivované.

Už vidím, jak by mne ředitel Deníku N znovu označil za konspirátora a šmejda.

https://t.co/yXFyWFv1dm

Pojďme se tedy s Jindrou Šídlem zasmát, jak je Rajchl neschopný a v souvislosti se můžeme zasmát i celému Dozimetru - hodíme tam porno, to lidi baví. Kdyby to nestačilo, lze si vzpomenout, jak se Rusové a Srbové rozhodli bez jakékoli účasti "hodnotových" marketérů zabít proevropského politika. Akorát, že vůbec.

Píší to ale Seznam Zprávy, renomované médium, šířící "pravdu a lásku", tak to musí být kvalitní informace, nebo snad ne?

Kvalitu bylo na Seznamu možné naposledy hledat tak před 3 až 4 lety. Dnes jde o nejhlubší dno novinářské práce v čele s Jindřichem Šídlem, Jiřím Nádobou a Marií Bastlovou. Zůstává jen osamělý Martin Čaban, jehož erudované analýzy vyčnívají jako zdravý strom uprostřed kůrovcem napadeného lesa.

Je to škoda, ale Seznam Zprávy se společně s Novinkami každým dnem propadají hlouběji a hlouběji do bažiny angažovaného PR plátku, podobně jako Deník N. Kdo by snad nevěřil, může si dva uvedené texty otevřít a kontext si nezávislé ověřit skrze dobové zdroje.

Buddha and Vedanta: Two Swords Cutting the Same Illusion

Vedanta says: “You are That.”

Buddha says: “There is no you.”

Now the real mystery begins.

The ordinary mind immediately asks: Who is right?

That is precisely where the mind has already gone wrong.

Vedanta and Buddha are not standing in two different realities. They are standing before the same illusion, but using different swords to cut it.

Vedanta says: Remove everything that is not you.

You are not the body—it changes.
You are not the mind—it comes and goes.
You are not your desires, memories, ambitions or fears—they are passing clouds.

And when everything false has been removed, Vedanta declares: the Self remains. Atman is Brahman. You are the ultimate reality you have been searching for.

Buddha walks into the same forest with a still more dangerous knife.

He says: “Do not even keep the idea of a Self.”

Watch the body. Watch the mind. Watch the thoughts. Watch the desires. Watch the ego saying, “I am watching.”

Then watch that too.

Buddha leaves nothing for the ego to possess.

Vedanta may say, “You are Brahman.”

Buddha remains silent.

Why?

Because the moment you say, “I am Brahman,” the ego can immediately make Brahman its property. The ego has become spiritual. It has put on saffron robes, learned Sanskrit, memorized scriptures—and it is still the ego.

So Buddha takes away even God.

He takes away the Self.

He takes away the metaphysical ground on which you could stand.

He leaves you groundless.

And suddenly, something extraordinary happens.

When there is nobody left to stand upon the ground, you discover that you were never separate from existence.

This is the meeting point of Buddha and Vedanta.

Vedanta says: Brahman alone is.

Buddha says: the separate self is not.

Read deeply and you may discover the same silence between the two statements.

One removes the world of illusion and reveals the Real.

The other removes the illusion of the person who wants to possess the Real.

Perhaps Buddha’s genius was that he understood the danger of spiritual ambition.

The worldly man says, “I want money.”

The religious man says, “I want God.”

But wanting God is still wanting.

The object has changed; the desire remains.

Buddha therefore does something revolutionary: he asks you to abandon the seeker itself.

No God to possess.

No heaven to reach.

No spiritual identity to decorate.

No future enlightenment to accumulate.

Just this moment.

Just awareness.

Just seeing.

This is the Middle Way—not a compromise between theism and atheism, but a way beyond the argument itself.

The theist believes in God.

The atheist believes in the absence of God.

Both still have beliefs.

Buddha asks: Can you live without belief?

That is the challenge.

Vedanta says, “Know the Self.”

Buddha says, “Find the self.”

And if you really look—without belief, without fear, without expectation—you may find something neither philosophy can adequately describe.

Perhaps Vedanta calls it Brahman.

Perhaps Buddha calls it Nirvana.

But these are only fingers pointing toward the moon.

The tragedy is that humanity has spent centuries worshipping the finger.

The invitation is to look at the moon.

Go within—not to find an answer, but to discover what remains when every answer disappears.

When the seeker disappears, there is no longer anyone asking whether Buddha was right or Vedanta was right.

There is only that which is.

And perhaps that is the ultimate silence:

Vedanta says, “You are That.”
Buddha says, “There is no you.”
Meditation says, “Be silent and see.”

And here Buddha gives the word God an entirely new meaning.

God is not a person sitting somewhere above the clouds. God means the fortunate one—the one who has awakened, the one who has realized himself.

Only man has the possibility of awakening into God.

I have watched two birds
leave the same branch
in opposite directions,
each carrying a little morning
inside its wings.
The branch did not follow.
It simply trembled awhile
beneath the weight
of what had been there.

Love comes like that..
without asking whether the season is kind,
without consulting distance or tomorrow.
It places its whole, unreasonable tenderness
into our ordinary hands
and calls that faith.
For a while, someone becomes the lamp
left burning in the kitchen
after every other room has gone dark,
and even loneliness forgets its old name.

Then the weather changes.
Not cruelly.
Only as weather does.
A road bends where neither heart expected.
A season asks more
than two people can give
and still remain gentle.
And suddenly you are learning
how to become separate
without becoming strangers.

Yet the body keeps its small knowledge:
how they liked the window open,
how much milk went into their coffee,
which silence meant stay,
the almost invisible tiredness
that entered their voice before sleep.
Morning comes,
and all that knowing wanders the rooms
like a dog no one has told
the door will not open again.

I used to call this failure.
I was wrong.
Some loves come as rain
to a field that has forgotten rain..
brief, 
complete,
already disappearing into the earth
while the roots beneath
are only beginning to wake.
The rain does not remain
to witness what it has changed.

Years later, 
something greens.
Perhaps only a tenderness
you cannot remember learning,
the way you now hold another person's sorrow
without trying to repair it,
the mercy with which you forgive
what once would have hardened you.
And somewhere beneath your ribs
there is still a small room
where winter enters
but cannot finish its work.

So if love finds you
in tall grass,
at an airport,
across an impossible distance,
or barefoot in an ordinary kitchen,
go toward it.
Do not ask the sky
to swear it will never change.
The sky has other work.
Love does not become more true
because it survives every season.

And if one day you must open your hand
around the one
you once believed you would keep,
open it gently..
as you would release a living bird
back into the enormous field.
Not because holding it meant nothing.
Not because leaving makes the love less real.
But because sometimes the last tenderness
we can give what we love
is not to turn our love into a cage.

Then let them go.

The hand will remember the warmth.
The branch will remember the weight.
The field will remember the rain.

Someone walks away.
The longing does not.

It stays
the way evening light stays trembling on water
after the bird
has disappeared beyond the trees..

not asking to be called forever,
not asking to be understood,

only shining
where something beautiful
once passed.

#InkByVKrish

This topic of the difference between the self-reflexivity of vimarśa and the self-luminosity of svaprakāśatva is quite interesting. The better way to understand it is to see vimarśa as a form of action: the absolute act of self-positing, which is also svātantrya (independence). This is why it has such a strong symbolic and conceptual affinity with the Word (Vāk), and more specifically with the form of the word through which consciousness posits itself: “I am.” That prakāśa and vimarśa are one and that there isn't any duality between them means that this act of self-positing is immediately self-revealed.

But when obscured by linguistic conceptualization, which generates duality, consciousness appears to posit itself in terms of a division between self and non-self, subject and object, which is the root of the entire dualistic construction of experience. And through identification with the non-self, consciousness comes to appear as though it no longer possessed this autonomy of self-positing and instead seems to be produced by extrinsic conditions (as it happens in the jāgratavasthā).

This is different from the perspective of Śaṅkara’s Advaita Vedānta, which regards action as merely an upādhi. Because Brahman is considered niṣkriya. However there are other forms of Advaita Vedānta like that of  Maṇḍana Miśra's, in which Brahman/Ātman is equated with Vāk, the Speech that it bears some resemblance. Here, all knowledge and action are Speech, and consequently all that manifests is either a pariṇama or vivarta transformation of Speech only: 

"By akṣara - 'the syllable' - we express (that Brahman) is the Speech (...); or else for that reason (akṣara - 'imperishable') it is expressed that it does not involve (real) transformation". (I.16)

"Or yet, by 'only the Speech that generated all the worlds, only the Speech that enjoyed, the Speech that spoke, etc.', the Speech is revealed as the universal ātman. Likewise, in the Vedic hymn to the Speech, it is shown that the Speech is the universal ātman, the universal sovereign. (...) Furthermore, the modifications are related to the original Form; why, the world is related to the form of the Speech so we know it as a real transformation or a phenomenal manifestation of the Speech." (I.17)

"... there is no knowledge (comprising) a mental formation that is not affected by the form of the speech; therefore, it is correct to say that it is only the main Speech that manifests itself in such and such a way. This is also the way of reasoning for a collection, like a forest, or things that don't exist like a ring of fire." (I.19)

"Since in any case the knowledge of the object to be known depends on the form of speech, any object to be known is known to be in relation to the form of speech; therefore, it is a phenomenal modification or manifestation of it, such as the vase by example (is a modification) of clay or how the moon (reflected) in a wave in the water is (a phenomenal manifestation) of the moon. " (I.19)

“- How is there continuity of (form of speech in all things)? - It is that (the world) is known through the knowledge of (speech) with which it is affected. (...) Now, when someone has a valid cognition of fire through smoke or some other means of knowledge, it does not take the form of smoke; so that, even for objects (known) by other means, valid cognition maintains the form of speech (...). Likewise, the impulse that children have for their mother's breast, while repelling something else, cannot exist if they do not have the valid cognition of 'that' (indetermined as it is): because when you do not know certainly if it’s a pole or a man you have (in front of you), you don’t have an activity based on either; (so that) there is no valid cognition that is not affected by the form of speech. (...) In these conditions, we know that the world that is understandable in the form of (speech) is its manifestation. "(I.18)
